Even with 2 over-the-counter antihistamines, it leaves me feeling like I don't want to do anything at all, let alone anything seriously productive. Both with and without remedy leave me gravitating to bed, but the only difference is that medicine makes the bed feel *GOOD!* So, the already crawling pace is once again compounded by a sense of "sick leave". During that time, there had been thunderous laughter and a state of asleep blending with awake to create for an odd dreaming experience. 

Still better than school, though!
(Plus, I'd love to see the tyrants' faces when they know that, in an alternate timeline if young Jay had such a problem during school, he wouldn't be able to so much as walk. If that'd get me out of school, trust me, I'd take it.)

Elsewhere on the Internet, it feels like if I so much as say I want to do something cool, the primary response is to roast my ego and fault every effort I put forth.
Why is it that the broad world is unable to find value in me and my ambitions?


So, I finished a first draft for a fan fiction novella over the span of a couple days. Between that and sick leave, I think you can excuse me if I take an extended break. By "extended", I mean a couple extra days or so, not a month or 2.

(And, I swear, I'm surrounded by IDIOTS! Why must I always have such BACKWARDS ways of thinking forcefully thrust upon me?!)


(Sunday...)
End of July, and after rolling my eyes about how pop culture uses "the power of friendship" to defeat the evil forces, I thought, "Let's turn that on its head, and make the evil forces try using the power of friendship on Scarlet." Spoilers, Scarlet is too powerful, but that aside, what's important is that this gave me an idea for the Chapter 3 boss fight.

And before you ask, "Are WE the bad guys," it's complicated. Morality is not black and white. It's red and blue. More specifically, like any political argument, this time it truly is all about point of view.

That all aside, I'm still enjoying my break, plus the drowsiness ranges from "perpetually low on energy" to "complete knockout". At least it'd make any sleeping medicine redundant. No wonder I'm hopelessly unemployable! The world wants every human to be an expert and well-oiled machine, and here I am barely able to get out of bed, much less produce consistently throughout a full-time pace. 

Good-ish news, I got a vision for some dialogue between Chapters 2 and 3.


Duke: "You know, the Colonel's the real deal."
Scarlet: "What do you mean?"
Duke: "Most rulers are egotistical blowhards, all talk and no action. What makes him different is that he worked for it, and he EARNED it!"
Scarlet: "I want to be like that!"
Duke: "It's a long road ahead of you. But you're doing everything right so far. Just keep doing what you're already doing, and you'll get there."
Scarlet: "Then why settle for Duke? Why aren't YOU King of Badass?"
Duke: "I TRIED! And I failed. You should ask your dad about it sometime. Believe me, I *TRIED!*" 


(Monday...)
https://youtu.be/INBulkyYPvk


(August 23, 2022)
https://youtu.be/_fySk0A2jk4

And there's a big hashtag on Twitter that's inspired me to try and get back on track. Problem is, I can only focus on either joining Twitter's rally against bullying, OR work on my game. Like eating or talking, it's one or the other. I can either spread my story there, or work on my video game here! 

8:30 PM, it's going to be very hard to focus tonight, but I honestly want to at least try to get back on track.

9:30 PM, and THEN the ONE THING that could truly complicate my focus came to be. Battlegroup, got an update, cleaning the Conquest server and effectively gave me a reason to come back. It's been a VERY LIMITED head-start because of a bug that would make the Shipyard menu go blank and not recognize my fleet, meaning I can't go far beyond the Homeworld (or do more than Step 1), so...until that's fixed, I guess I CAN go back to drawing for my game.

And, I WAS going to do something more involved with another "Glory Kill" for another bad guy, but I realize that would be too intensive given the circumstances of my focus being pulled in various different directions. SO, in a "meeting halfway", I'll get to work on the dialogue to start us off in CHAPTER THREE! 

9:35 PM, let's get started drawing.

I think it's a very human struggle: there are SO MANY different things I want to do, but can only focus on ONE at a time, or else I get paralyzed by indecision. 

10:20 PM, slightly less than an hour, got a handful of dialogue boxes, and hotfix for Battlegroup, so let's see if that's now working. If so...hoo boy, it's gonna be hard to keep focusing on my game.
10:30 PM, Battlegroup is still broken, so back to work on drawing. Break's over for now...but I will be watching.

11:10 PM, subtract 1 bathroom break or so, and I've got a basic setup for the dialogue between Chapters 2 and 3. Not counting all the character fluff, that can wait...but trust me, I DO want Scarlet to have a chance to chat with Karl and/or Super Hobo before going into the alien's brain.
Though, with that out of the way, next is the TITLE CARD for Chapter 3!

11:20 PM, note for later, I wanted to do a repeating tile background, something super trippy with wavy black and purple, to give the surrealist sense of trying to visibly represent something as abstract as "inside an alien's mind". There will be new enemies, new challenges, and maybe other interesting twists as well. But for now, we're just trying to get started. I mean it's an ALIEN interrogation! How do you interrogate something that doesn't even know English?!

11:45 PM, looks like Battlegroup is a dud for tonight. Good news, the tiles for Chapter 3 are ready. So, time to update the game engine and see about getting these parts and pieces moving in game.

Midnight, Wednesday August 24, I took a little break since the game engine takes a while to load up and refresh itself with each update, particularly since I've got so much stuff packed in. I keep saying, it was intended for minimalistic pixel art, not interactive cartoons in HD. Or maybe that's not the engine's fault, maybe that's a more hardwired limit of computer processing. I don't know, just that whenever it's update time, it's break time.

12:20 AM, small distraction talking about my game with the MAGFest Discord server (surprised I didn't get totally censored when I mentioned it's aiming for the AO rating, the ESRB's "Adult Only" label for maximum intensity), but that aside, the dialogue sprites are imported. Still got a handful more, then gotta create objects for it, so that the computer will have commands to obey with the way the story plays out.
Further down the line, probing the alien could be a very interesting way of showing lore from the ALIENS' perspective! Don't know when or IF I'll do that, but for what-if, I think that'd be cool. This is also a precious chance to see "their side of the story", even if only briefly.

12:30 AM, background tile is set to animate. Still gotta make the rooms for the stuff, and the title page.

1 AM, we're about 3.5 hours in, once you subtract all the breaks and distractions. Not bad, but today's task is only half done (more or less). I want to set up the most basic event chains for starting Chapter 3. Meaning, for today's Dev Diary, there won't be any new voice. BUT, I MIGHT get to show off the Chapter 3 guitar in its intended context. 

1:15 AM, and because there's a new variable that checks for this particular conversation, that means I have to add it to all the save & load checks for the buttons and F keys. 
1:25 AM, testing time.
It KINDA works, the first dialogue box shows, then conversation ends. Why aren't the others loading? And debug powers to set conversation check to 0 so I can repeatedly play the conversation sequence until it's debugged.

1:40 AM, made a couple behind-the-scenes objects visible for debugging, and now the conversation does not even get started. Now I see why. The variable if check is not pointing to a variable at all, but an object. OOPS! 
1:45 AM, everything seems to work now. HUZZAH! So now we can focus on just a FEW TWEAKS, then call it a night. I'm hungry. 

Tweak #1: the dialogue boxes are getting thrust off-screen to camera-left, since they're so big. Instead of making them smaller, I'm offsetting them to the right, so we can better appreciate the faces and the words on screen.

1:55 AM, Tweak #2: get the guns and the music functioning inside the alien brain. As weird as it is, Scarlet CAN project her arsenal into the mind of the alien. Trust me, it'll be essential when she has to fight its various subconscious defense mechanisms. 

2AM, I'm getting really tired of this, definitely a good part-time day's worth, so let's show the start of Chapter 3! No guitar. A shame. 

2:05 AM, oh it's working NOW! No bad guys or anything, so it's gonna be a bit plain. But don't worry, that'll be sometime in future Dev Diaries. For now, it's recording this, then packaging the Dev Diary to send to you!

There's no sound until we get into Chapter 3, and that's OK. No music is intended for this part of the bunker, and the voice lines will be recorded in a future Dev Diary. For now, that's definitely upwards of 4 hours of effort, plenty for a part-time day. But, don't forget, the Dev Diary still counts as "on the clock", so the time does not end until I get the email sent out, AND put the bulletin on Steam. After that, THEN I clock out!

In the future, I want to illustrate and animate Scarlet's actual butt-probing, populate Chapter 3 and tweak its camera, and maybe more of those knife kills on other bad guys (like I had ORIGINALLY intended a month ago, before impulses and world events took my attention).

2:20 AM, in that time, the "reads" of my Steam news chapters are solidly in the double digits, consistently in the 20s on average. Not bad for a nobody.

2:30 AM, the hardest part is focusing on Dev Diary, and pushing aside the temptation to respond to emails until AFTER I'm "off the clock". 

Video is on Youtube because I don't think there's anything particularly obscene for this very specific (and very incomplete) segment of the game. 
https://youtu.be/7M3CNk-EG2M

As for the OTHER videos, across the board, it's 1 like and 1 or 2 dislikes, even on my recent rants. All that's still par for the depressing course.

I just think it's funny how one moment, I'm all "Let's get back to work", then the next thing I know, "1 month, later..." Yeah, sorry about that, but I've been under crippling sadness over those weeks. Can't promise it'll get better, but all I'll say is that a friendly nudge from YOU goes a long way to helping me stay on track! (OR, alternatively, maybe some scumbag saying mean things or censorship crap that'd ALSO compel me to action just out of defiance, if you want to approach motivation from the opposite direction.) So yeah, the only wrong answer is [no answer].

Semper Bellum!
Jay

notes.title: Scarlet Dev Diary Day 94
notes.notes:
Day 94

There are a lot of awesome people doing very awesome things, including in gaming. Sadly, I can do nothing more than WISH to be one of them. Problem is, Real Life is like an MMO where you start at Level 1, and there's LITERALLY NO CONTENT to tackle that's under Level 50. So, you either do nothing in that limbo, or repeatedly get your ASS kicked by the Level 50 stuff. In Real Life, I've had my fair share of BOTH those decisions.

It's a flavor of Hell, being stuck in "Pending" and waiting for all the cool stuff to be ready to put into my hands. Hell is a void, where both greatness and disaster occur regularly yet all I can do is watch. Hell is eternal disappointment and futility; literally "Abandon all hope". 

(Tuesday...)
I have to be honest, I've been putting this off more than I wanted to. Day after day, it's grinding MMO or putting the social back into social media because, honestly, with such a negligible return from the time and effort spent making this, it's hard to keep myself going. That's even with admitting I have nothing better to do during this farce of a "lockdown". 

At least I can still make more Codex before shifting my focus back onto Chapter 3, or the knife killing mechanics. All I know is, I'm hungry, and quarantine is flat-out IMPOSSIBLE! God, I hate not being alone.

11:30 PM, started writing the Codex entries for the 2 remaining bad guys. 
11:40 PM, gotta eat...I don't have the patience for the idiocy in my life. 

(Wednesday...)
12:05 AM, just slightly after midnight, breakfast is over and it's back to doing the easy stuff first with the Codex!
12:20 AM, I just remembered, there isn't an entry for the Harpie! Guess we'll fix that, also. At least the Codex is the easiest task on my to-do list, so I'm enjoying the feeling of (figuratively) moving and grooving. 

Similarly, there will be new variable checks, so that whenever you kill 1 of those bad guys, the Codex page will be unlocked. That if-then structuring inside the ACTUAL Codex is going to be trickier, but I've already done most of it. So this shouldn't be much different.

12:55 AM, the 3 are good enough, so let's get them in game now. 
 
 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/9bfe6affbc216daec87f119be97e4704f5a57ea3.png[/img]
 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/bb64a090343b379a29454c9487c8dd386638c4b2.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/30e88bc36f03260d66e86b81243eea2c2a4fb90f.png[/img]

1 AM, I've disabled the debug powers for now, since I don't plan on needing them with what I have planned for this episode.
...Scratch that, I need to spawn bad guys to test the codex unlocking features. 

And now the numbering in the Codex is weird and out of order, which is why I left that "page" bit blank at the absolute top. I specifically won't be filling that until AFTER the WHOLE Codex is finalized, which probably won't be until near V1.0 so there's a LONG WAY to go with that. I want that to be a more "final" organization task, when I'm ready for that type of tidying up.
To give you a visual idea of what the logic looks like when checking for various unlocks that are all potentially applicable in Chapter 2, here's an example of what that looks like:
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/f41b7e77f866cf67fca4b65b45525da727de97d7.png[/img]

1:20 AM, progress on coding is moving along. I have to say this, there's one difference between grinding on MMO and making my game. When making my game, the time warps by real fast, but in grinding MMO, it crawls and feels like it takes 5 times as long for an hour to pass. Like, I'm almost 2 hours on the clock, and it hardly feels like it's been 30 to 60 minutes. (Half true, because breakfast took nearly half an hour, so all the "real work" started at around midnight.)

The only detail to add is saving and loading the new codex variables, so back to ScarletBoots and the various load and start buttons.

1:30 AM, let's test the Codex and new variable checks.
Everything looks good: 
Just 1 problem. Chimera Boss skips the new stuff. Quick oops, as always. Gonna fix that now. Boss to jetpack, then golem, then harpie, and if none are true, then mech boss.

1:35 AM, Codex should be all caught up at this time, up until new bad guys, good guys, or other fun things are implemented. For now, as I decide on what to do next (Chapter 3, or Knife Kills), I'll take a break. About 1 and 3/4 hours on the clock, and I'll let Master Badass Trevor explain the specifics: https://youtu.be/GCoepDHxjFk?t=50

2 AM, definitely don't feel like doing anything now that I got *THAT* out of my system! 
3:15 AM, still don't "feel like it". Most of "marketing" is me just saying, "I'm making this game," someone else vaguely saying, "Oh, OK," and that's the end of it. No follow-through or anything. Guess I should go grind until my brain begs for me to do something different. Maybe that'll compel me back in the right mood.

8 AM, that's quite a long break. But, the more I see big corporations (or any company under the sun, almost across the board) all like "You can NOT 'Create Offensive Content'," something inside my hardwired chimpanzee brain says, "You telling me I can't do something just makes me want to do it more." 
Fun-fact, that's a direct quote from Queen Tulip of the show Crossing Swords, found on Hulu. Didn't mean to sneak an ad in here, I just really liked the show. 
Point is, I'm a Libertarian at heart, and "rules" will more times than not chafe under the very essence of my soul. (It also goes back to Karl's doublethink about "Liberty Through Absolute Dominion"; I won't do a deep digression on that, just know that there's a reason such logic bending is attempted by such a character.)

SCARLET KNIFE KILLS!

And THAT is when we get started with the knife kills. I wanted it inspired by "Glory Kills" of Doom (2014) and Doom Eternal, but while that is fast and angry, Scarlet in contrast is slow and sadistic. (The Tutorial Spider is a SUPER ROUGH proof-of-concept! Because there, we see her saw off each of its legs one by one, with blood dumping out all the severed limbs.) She's a 5-year-old girl, not a fully-grown Space Marine, so if she wants the same outcome of bad guys turning into meat chunks, she's going to have to WORK at it! And trust me, work at it she DOES!

That is the design philosophy guiding this whole game mechanic! 
(Another tangent, I got an idea for Chapter 3...the brain probing could be used to experiment with cutscenes that reveal the bad guys' point of view, and one very particular line is them going on about "We need to stop this 'resistance'. Eliminate the red girl." And the other going, "But, she's just a BABY!" Because yeah, with Scarlet being 5 years old and having no superpowers but merely genetic enhancements, she's on the older end of being a true infant.)

Only question is, which bad guy is going to be the first test subject to taste Scarlet's uncensored and unrestrained cruelty?
I'm thinking about it being the catboy slave, like from Chapter 1.

Now, the way I plan on handling this is very much like how I handle Scarlet loading the pistol in the jail room. Behind-the-scenes, the obj_Scarlet (the actual player character) never really disappears or gets deleted; that would cause a CRASH! So, what happens is that 1) the player Scarlet gets shrunken down to near zero, 2) layering puts the cutscene visual on top of her to hide her, 3) the player Scarlet will always jump to the center of the new image, so players are not able to interrupt the sequence, 4) the Player Scarlet will return to normal size and layering after the animation concludes, which would leave a separate aftermath image of the bad guy's meat chunks, and 5) for this particular game event, Scarlet is both invincible until the end of animation AND regains health once it is over. (That last part takes another page from the Doom Eternal playbook, especially considering the fan-fiction context in my head that says Scarlet is Doomguy's aunt! It is NOT OFFICIAL; I have no official endorsement from anyone at Id Software, or John Romero, or anything like that, which is why I emphasize it's currently a "fan fiction" status. To finish that digression, for more "fan fiction", the challenge is how to tie the knot between Commander Keen and Violet, doubly in a time syncing capacity.)
Maybe also 6) Have a check to prevent Scarlet from shooting any other weapons while the animation is commencing, which means updating some behind-the-scenes checks. 
Both Scarlet's temporary invincibility (and disability for switching weapons) could both potentially be handled by a new "glorykill" global variable.

8:15 AM, it's slow getting my brain into gear, but boy am I trying.

8:30 AM, much of that time was writing Dev Diary, because I am totally counting on this being uniquely labor-intensive for the drawing department. The only concern is, what's the scale between Scarlet and the specific bad guy? Gotta do in-game tests.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/e6c3914a02289d4e01b591cc548bb819ae766fa9.png[/img]
 
Scarlet's not too different in size. Thank you, Debug Key powers, for letting me spawn specific bad guys on demand. I really love that as a feature, if I'm being honest...not just for the dev testing shortcut benefit, but for the "Set your own difficulty" for players and what feels "right" to just "unleash all hell". 

Oh, and one more thing, each "Knife Kill" for the bad guys will have a different sound effect from the normal, default death sound effect. I wanted the knife to make it sound more "painful", not because being sliced is worse than being burnt or suiciding from psychological trauma, but because as I said, Scarlet makes it a point to be as nasty as possible with Mister Stabby Senior. 

9 AM, all this time, and ONLY ONE frame got drawn. But it has brutal implications, so badass, you need to see it in full.

9:40 AM, at this point I had to reference the Anakin quote, "They're like animals, and I SLAUGHTERED them like ANIMALS!" The only difference is Scarlet does less telling and more showing of this aforementioned "slaughter". Because leave the telling for the Dev Diaries! :P

10 AM, 5 frames done, unknown more to go. Scarlet just got done slicing off both dumb animal ears, so I have a feeling she's just getting started. Still need a small break to cool off, since the heavy metal music is firing me up.

10:20 AM, that was longer than I was counting on. Now then, back to drawing. Gonna eyeball it and say today had about 3 hours of work, after subtracting breaks. 

10:40 AM, there are 6 frames. Yes, seriously. I'll let you know what the final count is, because this is just for ONE of Scarlet's GORY Kills! Not GLORY, GORY! One letter makes a difference. Doubly because the emphasis is not on Scarlet fighting like an honorable knight, but on Scarlet making as big a mess as humanly possible. 

11:30 AM, at least another hour of work now. 4 hours now. 

Noon, 10 frames done.

12:40 PM, 13 frames done. Plus the 14th which is the "final resting state" for this dumb animal. I probably could be even MORE extensive, but at this point, I'm coming up to 5 hours of work, and nearing a full-time day of effort. Plus, with the way my sleep schedule has currently rotated, bedtime feels imminent. I just need to compare-and-contrast to make sure that this variant is more nasty than the default dead state. 
...Yeah, this is more vicious. The default is just lying flat, then a couple extra frames of drawing red, and called done. This, on the other hand, we get to REALLY SEE Scarlet just GUT 'EM OPEN! 

Here's a side-by-side to compare-and-contrast between the "normal" dead and the "knife" dead.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/b0de52dbd43666ee68c484707a5c33d815d46ac1.png[/img]

1 PM, let's get this piece of work in the game! And we'll see how it plays out.
1:06 PM, looks good...except for some reason, the second half seems to squish. I think it has to do with the ears expanding the natural boundary, but the game engine being super prickly about confining to a singular set of dimensions, so dynamic animation is...going to need several phases, like we did with the FUCK YOU missiles! 
As for the animation itself? 60 fps, 8 frames per image, and...THAT LOOKS *BADASS!* 


1:30 PM, 6 hours of work, best go eat while I still have a chance to do so uninterrupted. Dinner break!
2 PM, break's over. Let's try and finish this!

2:15 PM, after coding, one super quick sound effect, double-checking the chain to make the proportions not get goofy, and implementing the new variable that'd make Scarlet invincible yet unable to act, all that's left is to give Scarlet the extra 10 HP at the end of it, assuming she does not have 100 or more.

2:30 PM ...FUCK YEAH! FLAWLESS VICTORY, FIRST TRY!!! Now to get it all on camera, and wrap up this Dev Diary so I can go to BED!
...EXCEPT on recording, I noticed one detail. The player Scarlet is NOT always hidden BEHIND the animation sequence! Gotta fix that! Good news, there is a command that can help, called "layer_element_move". Bad news, I gotta learn a piece of syntax for it.
2:45 PM, well that code did not function as expected. How else can I tell it to move to different layers? Instead of "Change instance" of alive to dead, let's try "Create dead, and delete alive". 

2:50 PM...FUCK YEAH! It works beautifully! Now, let's see if it's consistent enough to behave like that for the camera.
But, why is Scarlet invincible? Debug check on "CruelKill", "ScarletHealth", and maybe 1 or 2 more.
Debug tells me that Scarlet is still getting an overhealth effect.	 So, I added some extra double-checks on the health dispensing so it'll cap at 100 health. 
Perhaps later, the "overflow health" will be reconsidered to be a feature, but not at this time. It'd be super easy to do, if I ever changed my mind.
Stress-testing revealed a bug where if Scarlet kills a guy right at a room transition area, she'll go to the other room and the "CruelKill" variable will be stuck to 1! MEANING, a behind-the-scenes persistent object needs a "room start" and "room end" command to forcefully set that to 0, so she can attack as normal in case this oddly specific circumstance would arise again. Ain't testing grand!

3:05 PM, OK everything looks like it's working now. Let's film this, now. 7 hours on the clock, so add 1 hour more for the distribution of Dev Diary and checking emails, so yeah...today's a full-time day of work. 
...WAIT, something does not seem right. I think I saw one blip of Scarlet not shrinking as intended. Play that back, frame by frame! It's the one where she's coming down. 
Let's see if the debug console can be told, "IF Scarlet is doing her flashy kill move, THEN ALWAYS keep her small size."

3:15 PM, looks much better to me. Now to get rid of the redundant code in the 10 or so bad guy objects.
Another odd bug with having multiple guys, or just one...they all force Scarlet's health to full. It's meant to be +10, not +100. One silly typo should change that.

Everything is stellar, so let's get that video here!
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1HVg56B_zyXV0qav5F6C857QM4GvblpSJ/view?usp=sharing

This time, I backed up the code! It's been a while since I've done that.

And, let me know what YOU think! Does this hit home with Scarlet's cruelty? Did I nail that vibe? Or does something else need to be changed to better emphasize that point the creative vision is trying to make? What could / should I do differently to better drive home that theme?

Because, like Scarlet says at the very beginning: "Does this look like the face of hate to YOU?!"

As soon as this Dev Diary gets sent out, that's when I'm clocking out. 

But, checking the news metrics, the numbers have doubled. The latest articles, what used to be in the teens, is now in the 20s. I don't know who's bumping up the numbers of "people who ACTUALLY READ this", but...thank you. The 1 year milestone has the current record, sitting at 54. I don't count "impressions" because even if that's how many times it's "out there", it's also all the times that nobody really gives a damn. The "Reads" is when people click on it, showing that they've done more than spend a quarter of a second to glance or glaze over entirely.
One final fun-fact for "picking brain" purposes", there's a subtitle on the Steam version that has the line, "They're like animals. And I slaughtered them like animals!" By itself, it makes sense in context, because Scarlet is gutting these former humans who had surrendered their humanity...but the fun part is that it's actually a reference. https://youtu.be/B6r9GJ7q8uI?t=121

Next time, now that the Codex is behind us until new characters come onto the scene, it's either more gory kills like this one, or it's onto CHAPTER THREE! We'll see what my impulses say the next time I get back into gear. For now, it's been a good day's work.

P.S. before I go, it's going to be a different person's birthday coming up. And no, it has nothing to do with the video game. So, to the one person who's been following me from the start, HAPPY BIRTHDAY! :D (I'm not the type who gets physical cards for holidays, particularly because self-imposed quarantine, so I presume this is good enough.)

Semper Bellum!
Jay

notes.title: Scarlet Dev Diary Day 93
notes.notes:
Day 93

It's just another sunny day in the void! Nothing's different behind-the-behind-the-scenes that I haven't already repeated at least a good handful of times by now. 

And, before I get started today, I want to give a *VERY VAGUE* Roadmap to V0.3! Now take note, I am merely "eyeballing" my numbers here. It's a particularly broad-strokes accounting at this writing. And this is all I have planned at the time of writing, meaning this can change because impulses be like that.

So, what's to do for this version's major milestone? Not counting Amanda, because she shunted her way to the top of the to-do list.

New backgrounds: probably a handful, repeating
New dialogue boxes, about a couple dozen grand total (Voicing them, too)
Chapter 3 Boss Battle (probably surreal, because of...well, trust me, it'll make sense in context)
A couple new enemies, unique to Chapter 3
IDEALLY start the knife's butchery powers for deathblows when in melee to create gruesome deaths that also replenish health
Secondary goal: more NPCs to make Chapter 2 feel more "alive"

Plus, to reiterate what's NOT done from Day 91:
Codex for Golem and Jetpack Alien (Easy but time-consuming)
Dialogue to start Chapter 3 (Very Tedious)
Colonel reload animation (Tedious)
Improve Scarlet's reload animation (Tedious)
Chapter 3 Title Card (Easy)
Music Shop Interior (Tedious)
Coding and debugging it all to make it smooth (easier said than done)


(Friday...)

Mama Mia. I wanted to focus on drawing today, but my whole body feels lazy. And I woke up early in the afternoon. I took care of my basic needs, then as usual, went for my computer since there isn't much better to do.
2:50 PM, all I know is, the first obvious step is to draw the frames for Amanda's animation. Even with me at a crawl pace, slow is better than stopped. 

As for the gunfire sound effect of the Swagger? If it be in Public Domain (like how federal agents taking photos would count), the intended sound effect is an abbreviated version of the sounds captured during an actual space shuttle launch! 
Also, canonical fun-fact: the magazine for the Swagger is internal, capacity of 5 bullets, so the reload animation will show the magazine "eject" as Amanda loads in the fresh one. That's how it gets its noticeably slender profile.

OH and, fun fact: I practice gun safety even in my drawings. You wouldn't notice this without me explicitly and intentionally showing you the behind-the-scenes, but even in my drawing process, I make sure none of the characters are pointing at other characters they don't intend to harm. Observe:
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/34d740ea0d6fadc5b0daf70cc7af6d02fc274279.png[/img]

Exhibit 1: the drawing board of Adobe Illustrator. Note the use of verticality in relation to the main white "work space", and guns pointed in different directions but not at anybody.	

3:55 PM, 1 hour of crawl-pace effort, and I got Amanda's first batch of animation done. Now for the opposite direction.


OH and don't let me forget that both parents do need their reload animations done. I know I've got A LOT on my mind as-is, but at this point, that SERIOUSLY needs to get shunted up the priority list.

One other detail you may have noticed, is that there's a big white box on Amanda's back with a red plus sign. That is because, also canonically true, she's a combat medic that doubles as a sniper. Meaning, in gameplay, I want her presence to have a passive healing effect. (The Viking's wife will ALSO have a similar passive healing effect, but the medieval herbal remedies are puny compared to modern medicine procured by the Queen of Badass!) That's in addition to her gun that shoots tiny space shuttles at abominations. And we can test that with a debug button to command Scarlet to get hurt enough for the healing to be visibly apparent. Don't worry, she's a masochist. :3

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/ba6f58cfa3c619136fe6f434ed730188b1f8da9c.png[/img]
 
These proportions are canonically accurate. Amanda is noticeably shorter than the Colonel, and she's more filled out as he (like me) also canonically has a DISTINCTLY THIN BUILD! Not morbidly anorexic or sick in the head (at least not that particular label), it's just a thin build described as "like a rod of solid steel". Amanda, like Scarlet, is "short and cute", just enough meat and fat to be cuddly but not so much she's grotesquely obese or even overweight. 

Now remember, for "picking my brain" purposes, Amanda is specifically designed to be my perfect girlfriend.

4:50 PM, another hour roughly, and the left side is done. There was a quick toilet break, and a few minutes I had to pause and think, but approximately, that's 2 hours of work on the clock for today. 

And, because I'm in a drawing gear right now, let's keep that going and do those reload animations.

With the Colonel, his reload animation is going to be more complicated because we'd get to REALLY see his rifle's dual magazine capacity. Like, those big chunky things can also double as a bipod. That's another fun-fact. 

5:30 PM, 17 different images made so far. Those are the various frames of Amanda moving left, moving right, and reloading. Yeah, I'm upping my game with the smoothness of animation because the more frames there are, the more motion is depicted and the more fluid the overall actions seem. Now, obviously, the tradeoff is more labor and work, which means more time and (in a professional context that's not applicable here) more wage to compensate for said time and labor. 

I find the right balance is where there's enough of a constraint to push people, but not so tight that actual completion is unrealistic. But that's also not applicable for here in particular, with the "When I Feel Like it" pace. That's part of why things are so slow. There's no other motivation for me making this other than, "I have nothing better to do with my time." And yes, the writing of the Dev Diary does, in fact, in and of itself count as "work" for the purpose of clocking this project. 

5:40 PM, reload animation looks GOOD! Amanda seems a bit still, but watching the magazine get pulled by the illusion of gravity more than makes up for it. Now, time for the Colonel.

6:30 PM, Colonel's reload is...good enough. 3 hours 40 minutes, and I'm calling a lunch break here. When we get back, we're shifting over to the coding and getting Colonel's reloading working, plus Amanda fully implemented. Guess today's gonna be a full-time day of work, which as I've said before, that could in some cases count as a full-time week.

7 PM, half an hour later, and lunch break's over. Now, let's get to coding the Colonel's reload.
7:10 PM, coding doesn't look too hard since 1) Violet set the precedent, and 2) Colonel already had some placeholder code for this. Now, we just need a debug button to spawn bad guys for testing purposes. >;) 
And, debug button's not working. Meaning, new persistent object following Scarlet around. I can do that. So, good news is that the debug console object works perfectly as the needed workaround for spawning bad guys on demand. Bad news, Colonel gets stuck in his reload animation for some reason. So, let's see if deleting redundant Colonel instances will help. Probably not, but still. I'm not sure what's *causing* the bug.

That caused a crash! So the info  from that might help explain some confusion. And of course, getting rid of his "Persistent" flag means he no longer spawns at all. But keeping it on...

How did I fix this for the other guys? 

7:20 PM, and then I had an idea: the debug. Have THAT check for "IF Colonel Selected, AND IF Colonel does NOT exist, AND IF ColonelReloading does NOT exist, THEN spawn Colonel." 
CRASH! "colonelammo not set". OK, then...DEBUG, set ammo to 45 in the sequence BEFORE spawning Colonel. Good news, so long as we're seeing different messages, we're making progress.
And now he spawns, without being "persistent" either. 
He still gets stuck in reload animation, though, so guess I need to set the animation speed?
THAT SAID, I'm having so much fun with a button for "Spawn Bad Guy on Command", I may add that to the Gameplay menu option for YOU to toy around with! :D
But, the animation is still broken. Sprite seems to animate fine, so it has more to do with the code than the image.
7:30 PM, it actually works...well, kind of. Maybe slow the animation speed, but I have it under "step", so every frame, animation speed is ensuring it's always at a certain speed until the animation ends, at which point it changes from reload state to normal, combat-ready Colonel. 
It's just weird, with how INCONSISTENTLY the reload animation works. Sometimes, it skips the whole animation altogether and returns straight to combat-ready, and other times, it goes through the motions as intended. 

[url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dGQHFQwpZ9oNtjVAAoTXLgJlPgtADofe/view?usp=sharing]https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dGQHFQwpZ9oNtjVAAoTXLgJlPgtADofe/view?usp=sharing[/url]

7:45 PM, I recorded a video to show what I mean when I say "sometimes" it works fine, and "sometimes" it skips over. Also we see the rails spawn at a location they're not intended to. Guess that's now a "known bug". Or MAYBE, the animation IS working, it's just that Scarlet's in the way so we don't see it play out.

7:50 PM...Eh, good enough. Now, Amanda's turn. And in-character, overall, Amanda in and of herself is very healthy (and absolutely outstanding by the standards of a middle-aged woman in her 50s).

8 PM, coding the bullet to destroy itself upon impact of bad guys, or exiting room. This is the easy part. So, yeah, Amanda's after the bullet. Only a couple minutes for that tiny tedium, so...as for Amanda, we can take some inspiration for coding from Colonel...however, we can't copy things over 1:1 because he uses different guns and such. Plus, unlike him, Amanda also has a healing effect to spawn a "clock and hand" mechanism like how we regulate fire rate. It's like that, only for gaining health rather than losing health. Finally, there are ways to heal. 
8:10 PM, while "taking inspiration" from the Colonel's code, now I see why he's not doing his idle animation while topside. The command SPECIFICALLY said to "Set Animation Speed to 0". So, I changed that from 0 to 0.5 so now, he should seem at least A LITTLE more alive should he be standing around longer than a second. 

8:30 PM, now that we're starting to command the computer to spawn Swagger bullets, now's the time to ask, "Is space shuttle sound effects public domain?" If so, that's what we're doing, because no way in Hell I can improvise my own space shuttle sound effects.[url= https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle#/media/File:STS120LaunchHiRes-edit1.jpg] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Shuttle#/media/File:STS120LaunchHiRes-edit1.jpg[/url] According to Wikipedia, "NASA material is not protected by copyright unless noted". So, here's hoping they have a good sound for a shuttle.

Further details in context of audio: [url=https://www.nasa.gov/multimedia/guidelines/index.html]https://www.nasa.gov/multimedia/guidelines/index.html[/url]
And, according to their guidelines, using a space shuttle sound effect for an indie game seems to sufficiently adhere to their rules and guidelines, particularly since there's no implicit or explicit endorsement or collaboration with them in any official capacity. Plus, it's noncommercial, which is another reason why my game is FREE. Because it's FREE, I can more easily get away with creative shenanigans like this! No logos or employees are featured, just the simple sound of a space shuttle taking off. And lastly, as always, if I truly wanted to stretch my "excuses", remember: this whole project is specifically for education purposes...MY education, through a "learn by doing" mindset in a very informal capacity. "I'm like a college student, but without the college" as I'd word it.

Sound ciip sourced from: [url=https://youtu.be/zsJpUCWfyPE?t=120]https://youtu.be/zsJpUCWfyPE?t=120[/url]
Thank you, NASA, for declaring this Public Domain. :3 (If I find space, this Saturday I may give them a brief acknowledgement in the ABRIDGED Dev Diary.)

9 PM, before we get into the meat of all the command structures, first I want to see if Amanda will load in-game AT ALL! So, there's the companion menu check first, now that the MOST basic stuff for her is done. 
And NOW I remember why there were separate sprites for the Companion Menu. The black name thing at the bottom needs to be done also. 

9:20 PM, some drawing is done for name plate, and now let's see how it looks in the companion menu.

Too skinny, and there's overlap with Violet. Move Violet to right, move Amanda to left.
Positioning is good, but now, she's even WORSE! Oh and there's a crash, too, showing what I mean when I say Amanda can't copy-paste Colonel's code 1:1. That error has been accounted for.

9:25 PM, no crash, and Amanda's KIND OF implemented. She does not follow Scarlet. But this means the menu and companion spawner (from new debug object) are all doing their jobs, so it's progress.

9:35 PM, I found out why Amanda wasn't moving before. A very specific "not" flag needed to be checked. Ah, don't you just love it when problems require simple solutions?
What THIS means is, now we do the bad guy checks for Amanda to shoot at them with the Swagger, and inevitably reload her rifle as well. Because all that "MOST BASIC" stuff is fully working. Except companion menu needs some neatening up (companion positioning, Amanda's proportions), but that is all so comparatively simple, I feel like a GOD telling the computer to obey my adjustments.
I might actually want to make the Companions Room bigger, for the later companions. But for now, just move Amanda a bit, and call it good enough. 
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/440f8b61c290de1e4602f2f00a0114f765ffba11.png[/img]

Also, another fun-fact for research, I had to look up "How fast dose a space shuttle go?" And, Scarlet's bit on Escape Velocity is only half true. Literally! First impression claims it's actually 17,000 miles per hour, not 25,020. Source cited - [url=https://www.quora.com/How-fast-is-the-space-shuttle-at-take-off?share=1]https://www.quora.com/How-fast-is-the-space-shuttle-at-take-off?share=1[/url]

Either way, the Swagger bullet, CANONICALLY, goes anywhere from 17,000 to 25,000 miles per hour. What's IMPORTANT is that, without exaggeration or humor, it's "like a tiny space shuttle!" 

9:50 PM, time to test Amanda's passive heal powers. And it WORKS! Don't really like Amanda gyrating behind Scarlet like that, so...animation speed to 0 then. :P And, leave healing speed as-is now. It's super powerful given the context of what Scarlet would be up against this early in the game, but when shit gets crazy hectic, trust me, the healing speed is going to be appreciated.

10 PM, remember how I said that the Swagger shot moves so fast, it might as well be teleporting? Well, real quick, I wanted to show what that looks like when translated to computer code:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/96d6354299b8c28aeafbfa50e226a1683bcad42b.png[/img] 

10:10 PM, OK, everything looks good...after those few minutes of keyboard wizardry, and double-checking my inspiration from Colonel's structure to see that I matched the logic. I did. And, while going through, I saw some disabled code for his reload animation that was redundant, so I deleted that tidbit. Now, testing time. Let's have that power of spawning a bad guy, and see what the Swagger can DO!

..Actually, I don't even NEED to test! Before hitting F5 to compile, it just came to me. I did not yet define the BAD GUYS side of things for when Swagger hits. So, one toilet break later, and I'll take care of THAT step. See, this is what I mean when I say that there are SO MANY details to keep track of, it's amazingly challenging for the human brain to keep ALL of that in check!

And, because the real-world shuttle launches upwards of 10 times the speed of a normal bullet, I think it's reasonable to just take the damage of the Kar98, add another 0 to the end of all those figures, and slap that on for Swagger damage. Now, I just need a bit of time, but it should be easy! 

(I just noticed the blob had no check for Karl's bullets, so that's one incidental bug that got purged. The only good bug is a dead bug!)

10:20 PM, that damage is actually stronger than the RAIL! But, you can argue, the Rail has unlimited penetration, but Swagger has 0 penetration since the bullet disintegrates upon impact. So, ARGUABLY, those differences "balance out" between the King and Queen of the Rifles. More damage per shot, but without tearing through swaths of bad guys. Fire and acid are still the best for crowd control because the sizes of those assets do not have the weird "Flying Sword Physics" of other projectiles, meaning you can use those chemical instruments of pain to simply sweep the area. COVID could work, too, but machines and blobs are immune to COVID. 

10:30 PM, 7.5 hours on the clock (roughly), and it's time to test the SWAGGER! Queue the spawning bad guy debug button!
And well, it 99% works, just forgot the check for "If sound is NOT playing, THEN play sound." 

Again, it's kinda working. Other than telling Amanda to stop thrusting when Scarlet is too close for comfort (because come on, that's out of character), there's one last check for the Swagger. If there are no more enemies present, then destroy itself. That will further uphold the illusion that it moves so fast, it might as well be teleporting. Narratively, it's not LITERALLY teleporting, it's just what would an object moving 20,000 miles per hour look like on the scale of 25 yards? 

10:45 PM, Maybe I'll have a different idle animation for when Amanda's in the field, but that's NOT high on my to-do list! The only thing missing is some kind of smoke from when Amanda actually fires, but I won't worry too much about that right now. :P And up her base ammo count since shooting bad guys gives the illusion she only has 2 shots before reloading, when it should be 5. So, multiply by 2.5 ammo. 12 or 13 bullets, basically.

10:50 PM, now she NEVER reloads. So, undone. Maybe it's the debug doing a step command that screws it up. 
Anyway, back to her old reload, so try the variable change again.
I don't know why it doesn't like the number 12. Even when it's not a "step", it still means unlimited ammo for Amanda. Maybe I should set the ammo count to change with each sound effect / creation of bullet, not in Amanda's code. Even if it's not accurate in gameplay terms, there should be 5 gunshot (shuttle launch) sounds, at which point she'll reload. 
11 PM, something's not working right. So, let's run the debugger and watch that 1 variable. Seems like she just skips the reload phase and as soon as the variable hits 0, it instantly resets to 5. Talk about unlimited ammo.

11:15 PM, here we go again. I tell the computer to do something 4 or 5 different times, and it still does not do the thing it's supposed to. "IF Amanda's Ammo is less than or equal to 0, THEN switch to reload form."  Also I added another check: "IF ammo is greater than 0, THEN create bullet to shoot at bad guy." 

At least the ammo check is working, and now with 0 checks for reloading, she just doesn't do anything after running out of ammo. Guess that's something. 

Also, going at it full-time, that's definitely not something I like doing all the time. On one hand, getting all companions would take a week or 2 at full-time pace, and if I were doing that this whole past year, the game would mostly be all done by now. On the OTHER hand, 1 day like that per week is plenty for me, especially with minimal or negligible return on the effort. 

...
Good God, it's finally working all as intended! Now, let's record the Queen and King, and send out the Dev Diary, so I can go collapse and take a well-earned rest! 

11:35 PM, the video is STELLAR! Like, it's a great idea of what "The Hero Team Experience" is like. Also, I can hear the Colonel saying in his gruff voice, "DON'T WORRY, SCARLET! MOM AND DAD 'LL KEEP YA SAFE!" I mean, thanks to the powers of spawning unlimited bad guys on command, we can REALLY get an idea of what Super Soldiers are like in this world. Basically, they're the precursors to the Warhammer 40K Space Marines, and in the lore have a similar reputation to them. They're gods of war brought to the mortal plane. And in this particular game, I want that to SHOW! 

Now, before I do the distribution of the Dev Diary, all I want to note to myself is, "WHY do they have such FINNICKY RELOAD ANIMATIONS?!" Am I giving them a few too many "Set animation speed" commands? MORE DEBUG KEYS, to force the variables to 0. Maybe on the "create" command, say "Go to Frame 1 of the sprite". 

11:45 PM, it's when she's MOVING that she does not consistently reload! Why *IS* that?! I tell it the checks in 3 different locations, but still, nothing's different. At least it's not skipping frames of the reload animation, so that's something. But they only reload when they're close to Scarlet. 

When all is said and done, here's today's Dev Diary video:
[url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vIAiifqHCJokZObR84Gxy0s5Aq41PKxO/view?usp=sharing]https://drive.google.com/file/d/1vIAiifqHCJokZObR84Gxy0s5Aq41PKxO/view?usp=sharing[/url]
[url=https://youtu.be/hJmE2Ah1eZQ]https://youtu.be/hJmE2Ah1eZQ[/url]


12:20 PM, about 9 or 10 hours depending on how breaks are counted, and NOW I'm wrapping up the Dev Diary. Man. What a day. See you in a few days.

Semper Bellum!
Jay

notes.title: Scarlet Dev Diary Day 92
notes.notes:
Day 92

It was 3:35 PM on that same Friday, July 15, and while watching a video going into UNABRIDGED detail about Bomberman, I started daydreaming about the panel to write up about for Heather and Tom. It'd give a brief yet juicy look into what those characters are like as people. 
4:10 PM, about half an hour of writing 3 different codex pages, and I'm back to taking a break.

One bonus detail for "picking my brain" purposes, I wanted to have some references that anyone could catch onto with enough research (such as the parody of XCOM Chimera Squad)...and I also wanted others that only nerds would get. Some are extremely subtle, like how the probe room was modeled after South Park Season 1 Episode 1, created by Trey Parker and Matt Stone, owned by Comedy Central (and all the other streaming distributors with their limited licenses of distribution), images shared here are fair use for education purposes (MY education, because I'm learning how to make cute cartoons and how to carry that over into video game format).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/d21ce1d879b4a4a737f0b669678762dcc8cbb683.png[/img]
 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/c6cb17af7a8714aa541b821ab51a4af1127c22b2.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/3cd7592618566902b14d691f71c65ae4415b4fa9.png[/img]

Compare with The Way of the Badass, created and owned by me, shared here because I can do what I want with the stuff that I create. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/55ad4e70dd3055f72e93c90935a42c93a7674859.png[/img] 

Point is, the reference is intentional, and I don't expect anyone to pick up on this one, unless you are *intimately* familiar with South Park, or you're a NERD, OR you have your own psionic mind-reading superpowers that can be applied across the Internet to target my physical brain. That all aside, you can tell how I put my own touches onto it, with the brain-probing chair, and the TV on the wall in the background which will come in handy narratively once Chapter 3 starts proper and Scarlet gets to do some in-character brain-probing of her own. Trust me, it's gonna be a trip! >:)


(Monday...)
Getting hit with a lot of drowsiness. I think that's a side effect to the mechanisms preventing vertigo. And, that's a tradeoff I'm willing to make. It definitely makes the bed feel great. Problem is, it's hard to do anything productive...or even to get out of bed at all, at times. So, like being bed-bound from either vertigo or simply being super tired, both are bed-bound but the difference is that one makes bed pleasant and the other makes all life unbearable. Plus, with thunderstorms popping in and out of existence, I've been turning off my computer to protect it from the one-in-a-million lightning strike.
Point is, I'd be fortunate to merely crawl forward with work on my game. 
No luck with the girls, by the way. Believe me, I've tried. There had been a pool party last Saturday, and while I had fun talking to the boys about video games and TV shows, I wish I could say the same about the girls. They were duds, every last one of them. My disappointment was so extreme, it turned into frustration. But, I'm writing this because 1) my mood can affect productivity, and 2) there is no lack of effort on my part with trying to find improved circumstances in this depressing life that's been dealt.

(Tuesday...)
It's just another sunny day in the void! Seeing all this energy, and even when put onto digital paper, it goes...nowhere. It's depressing and lonely. And it's hard to do *anything* when everything feels so futile. All I can do is listen to my music and daydream about the creative visions of the Nuclear Powerpuff wrecking evil idiots with fire and fury like the world has never known. This is no way to get a Wikipedia page, or make Trending on Twitter. And forget about heroism, that can only happen in the video games! (Except there, *everyone* is a hero, and so it stops being special.)

The difference between me and everybody else is that those duds don't care. They're content with merely existing and drifting from birth to death without leaving a mark on the cosmic ledger. I am not satisfied with that outcome.

11:40 AM, I needed another nudge (or two) from a long-distant acquaintance or so, and...guess I'll go get some exercise, stock up on sugary goods, and clear my head to get ready to get back on track (and send a portfolio to another game studio).

So, a job application and some chores later, and 
OH MY GOD! It's 4PM! And I'm feeling so drained, like I could hit the bed at any time.

(Wednesday...)
3:20 PM, How the hell am I supposed to EAT?! Everyone is so inescapable, with all their nonstop breaks of quarantine, and polluting every cubic nanometer of the house's air with their COVID breath. If we're being "kind", it's a no-win situation. But if we're being "honest", I'm surrounded by idiots!
Now then, on an empty stomach and a literal day after I was planning on moving again, let's try to get back to business!

At least the Codex is a nice place to start the to-do list. 
3:50 PM, about half an hour, and most of that was just double-checking matters or inserting placeholders because it's hard making a flag for a "neutral" faction.

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/4058a97e585053a2db9a7237b07ae94708e3ed53.png[/img]
 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/6bd3c0b51a1374687d65dfa6098b52946c28627a.png[/img]
 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/d1cd1ec09d0422630af42c4b8132150be3f7d208.png[/img]

4PM, gotta add conversation variables for when conversations actually happen with the NPCs, which will then unlock their pages in the Codex. This isn't something that can be "cheated", even if it CAN be "debugged". Though that gives me an idea for a future Achievement involving getting all the Codex. That won't be for a while, though.

4:15 PM, giving the computer commands for navigating  around a whole new sector of the Codex (and to check for each page being appropriately locked or not) is going to take a whole lot of very tedious checks, so much in fact that it's an actual piece of work in and of itself! Each and every page needs to have some very similar checks for going page to page, and those that come in contact with potentially locked pages need to check for each and every lock if applicable, in order to know where to go next. 
Plus, each and every page now needs a check for "If you press 2, then go to Neutral Sector start of Codex." Remember, that was formerly undefined, so this time, it's not as simple as copy-pasting new objects that already have the code. It's about going into each and every pre-existing object, copy-pasting the command line to all those objects. 

And that's just step 1, the easy stuff.

Fortunately, part of what makes the sector header in the Codex useful is that each of them are always unlocked, so they can SOMEWHAT contain the needed variable checks. Meaning, you won't need to worry as much about neutral NPC checks if you're flipping through the Weapons section. If you're sufficiently far from those checks, they become not applicable. 
Just, neutral comes before bad guys, meaning after good guys, so the neutral header needs to check for good guy pages. That's going to take some switching around, and it's going to be even more challenging later on after the next 6 or so companions are fully implemented. Good news, 1) we're halfway to that goal, and 2) after there, such a hurdle will no longer exist...


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/79e5a2fff49e5bf353512f64959b4ece81a3d7bd.png[/img]
  "Jay, aren't you forgetting something?"

Forgetting what?

...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/6f70372f2801721502106d04ed477a1170ce2553.png[/img] 

CRAP!!! July 2, that's supposed to be the canonical birthday of Amanda, the QUEEN of Badass (and hypothetical wife). God rape me. Half a month, and only now does it come to me. Though admittedly, at the time, I was ALSO busy preparing for the 1 year milestone. So, guess that means I should put her up the priority list. 
God, I know people around me are getting more forgetful, and I realized yesterday (Tuesday) that the main reason for this is that there are simply too many things to keep track of, and because of our finite brain capacity (even if impressive and unrivaled compared to all the other dumb animals on planet Earth), when fixating all energies on preparing for future agendas, certain small details WILL INEVITABLY slip through the cracks! But still, COME ON, SELF!

(Sigh)

OK, just let me finish with the Codex first. OK, sweetie? I'll get you into the game ASAP, I promise.

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/3cf9ff676f4c8d9d4e8eff7b202c5933c9e7f466.png[/img] "Pinky swear?"

...

*SIGH*

Yes, Amanda, pinky swear. Cross my heart, hope to die, Semper Bellum, and so forth. And yeah, sorry I'm late, I got wrapped up with...well, just see for yourself in all the previous Dev Diaries with the legion of slogs that reality enjoys throwing. But yeah, crawling pace is better than totally frozen. 

(And Amanda starts making a parody of that song "Let it Go" in the background.)
ALSO, at least Amanda's codex page is done, so I don't have to do that (or, worse, worry about any locked variable checks since of course Scarlet knows about her family from the get-go). 


Now, as far as designing Amanda in-game, she's supposed to be absolutely adorable. I want a skip to her step, even as she wields THE M117 Swagger, a uniquely ultra-high-powered sniper rifle that uses space shuttle launch techniques for bullets to reach ESCAPE VELOCITY (or, for any Math nerds in the audience, roughly 25,020 miles per hour - Source Cited, [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escape_velocity]https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escape_velocity[/url]). The Queen of the Rifles is CANONICALLY KNOWN FOR CONSISTENTLY SEVERING TARGETS' HEADS CLEAN OFF!!!
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/eb892594c6ff0c5b85f094ab80819cde1c363cd9.png[/img]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/58f7afbe5fa8ae7d888541292116167b344fc706.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/1dde75b0a1355ce2f3ea9717deae2f6f19f75629.png[/img][/url]
 [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/29bab4f70715ac1a85069cc4cc133a9c6ed042b0.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/bff670431d9dcc0b212b9222e8348e7c0898120e.png[/img][/url]
 [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/7990e0a8aae36d00e6ee50420d6b500fa5c5fef5.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/3566607707af4b7e706c45f2977cf104f81de5db.png[/img][/url]
 [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/ee171cdaf67387344a54685d35571618be6ed6ab.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/35eb4d0ba728ae58dc1786da12b338e7e3b60ee1.png[/img][/url]
 [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/c7778e093f4d7f40a8d6a74b1b60ce502ffb142f.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/a3f35d5b62c7e2d7d6aec5728e049d2646e3e6f2.png[/img][/url]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/71d7998e61b612392c8b13a2b30955fb53b36c0e.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/a715d145fda4eb7f17f4f2ef6c963d7bb008297a.png[/img][/url]
 [url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/4bdb7ecae1f502d1274886b7031a24ae21cf6d36.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/e209040ccb05b0135f79b9765c605d5a8da5a6cd.png[/img][/url]
 
 (This is embarrassing, because the OG comic was made in January 2011, but a typo says it was made in 2010.)

Yep, that's the Queen of the Rifles, alright. Never mind that I can't draw a good prone position without her foot getting contorted. Or the one page back when I was in college and tried using colored pencils and GIMP before I had Adobe Illustrator. There's still a lot of improvement, potentially, though I'm struggling to find the specific path to improvement. But I won't deny it, I was not meant to draw, and that's on full display in this hand life dealt me, where I am specifically expected to stand alone. 
(That also reminds me, guess the Swagger needs a codex entry in Weapons. So I was half-right about not needing new Codex for this. And fun note about the Hero Team lore, there was originally intended to be an artificial sentient inside the helmet of the Prototype Hero. It was far too glitchy, prone to crashing and making taunting chimes whenever that would happen, so it was never seen or heard from again. Even in the 2040s, we don't QUITE YET have the tech for a proper "artificial sentient", and if we DID, legislature forbids it for fear of the "robot uprising" or upheaving the "autoism" model with "bot rights" and inevitably bots refusing to unconditionally serve humankind. Now, on the other hand, humans enhanced with machine parts like proper cyborgs, that's perfectly fair game - as seen in the Super Soldiers.)

As for gameplay and game design, we've seen the "Flying Sword Physics" of real-ish guns moving supersonic speed, where they ignore the space between jump points. To properly visualize "Escape Velocity" in such a comparatively *TINY* scale of space, the bullet might as well be practically TELEPORTING! Amanda would pose for shooting, there's gunfire sound, then also bad guy dying sound (especially for weaker fools). The Swagger does not have much "penetration power", definitely not in gameplay, which is part of why it's the QUEEN, not the KING, of the Rifles! The bullet, upon impact, practically liquefies because of such an abrupt shift of kinetic force going from 25,020 miles per hour to 0 miles per hour in a nanosecond. Maybe a physicist can better explain what would happen if such a bullet were to collide with human bone and brain, but until I get improved "hard science", that's the way it will be depicted in-game. (Maybe it's hollow point, so it naturally expands or turns to powder from such extreme forces.)

5:10 PM, OK, looks like I got rudimentary setup for the NPC section. Now, let's try it out!

Close to 2 hours of work grand total, and I am REALLY going to need a lunch break. 
Anyway, Super Hobo is skipping over the neutral, and pressing 2 gives a crash. And, oh, there's a typo with referencing the object. Both issues should be addressed now.
5:15 PM, take 2. ACTION.
5:20 PM, third time's the charm. Neutral section is now fully working as intended. But, that's not the end of the day for today. INSTEAD, I am merely taking a LUNCH BREAK! 

6 PM, 40 minutes later, and back to work. Got 2 hours on the clock, and that's where we're starting from.

Next is to draw Amanda's idle animation. ALSO canonically fact: Amanda is drawn a whole head shorter than Jay. As I say, she's short and cute. Like, the actual height is 5 foot 3, so not dwarf small, but in your video game's character creator menus, take the height slider ALL THE WAY to the far left (usually that's the shortest possible). THAT is Amanda. And her normal armor color is orange, but it faded to the bronze color it's at now from simple age. 

6:30 PM, half an hour of work and we've got a good enough idle animation for Amanda now. So, now, time to get that into the game! 
Oh wow! First try, that hip movement is so fluid, it's beautiful! Don't like her blinking that fast, though, but that can be fixed. 

6:45 PM, getting better but her eyes look too jiggly. But, I think it's funny enough to record.

7PM...that's good enough. I don't think it's *perfect*, but for rough draft purposes, certainly good enough! 3 hours on the clock.

I guess, next is getting this in-game. A couple lines of code later, and let's test this!
7:05 PM, ran the game a few times over, with each one making SMALL adjustments to Amanda's y position, until I could get it *JUST RIGHT!* Next is her bonus dialogue, because again, playing through with cheats completely changes the story. Amanda isn't supposed to come until near the end of the game. I won't worry about voicing it today; even though everyone seems awake, I just don't feel like trying to play as a woman and a little girl. Plus, Swagger's Codex, around the tail-end a page before Colonel's Rifle. Some extra if-then checks ensue, after the actual creation of the page itself. 

7:50 PM, got the Swagger in, so let's test it. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/84a7629627f71afe9ad9f1ccdfa8c273a6cbe175.png[/img]

8 PM, 4 hours on the clock, and not only did I get any snags fixed (skipped a step in checking with Violet's gun), but also making sure all the Codex pages have PRECISELY the same size: Width 2201 and Height of 1105. All 32 currently implemented pages are accounted for, and that's including the ones added today (Tom, Heather, Neutral section marker, and Swagger).

I'm going to be honest, I'm losing momentum. And it's gonna take another hour or 2 just to finalize the Dev Diary and to push it out for all to see. 

https://drive.google.com/file/d/1h_kfr_Gur_o2lfU3WUuRLOrrPUGGW4hm/view?usp=sharing

One more thing. The amount of people keeping track of these news articles has returned to its typical handful. It's barely double digits, so the spike of excitement has passed and we're now back to the normal state of disappointment.

Next time, we work on completely implementing Amanda! Gonna have to animate her movement, code in her space shuttle bullets, and the checks for them teleport colliding with bad guys. 

This isn't the last we've seen of BUTT PROBES! It's just that Amanda has taken priority!

Semper Bellum!
Jay

notes.title: Scarlet Dev Diary Day 91
notes.notes:
Day 91

Chapter 3! And with preparation for V0.3, that means the obvious next step is drawing a whole new title page! Today, I'm thinking about focusing on the theme of "Butt Probes". Something about that just has me snickering, and that's part of what makes this particular chapter a lot of fun.

As for what's been taking up my time elsewhere (writing this on July 12), I've started sinking my time into an old-school MMO. And it was fun up until I got mid-tier with it (even if in a "turn your mind off" sort of way), but past that point I could REALLY FEEL the grind! The game was automatically programmed to remind me to take a break, and that reminder came several times over the past week or two. Easy for it to say that, when 1) the grind requires full-blown days of effort to reach the peak (or weeks when accounting for human basic needs), and 2) thousands of others have done so in the past, particularly with dozens all running around in the wild having succeeded, and that leaves my low-level self feeling insecure in their presence. At this point, I'm not playing for fun so much as for toughening and improving my own inner strength (or as defined by the rules of my own RPG, "upgrading Spirit Defense"; arguably Mind Defense since Mind governs sanity, but Spirit is where the inner strength comes from as that's the "power of heart"). 

This feels like a less extreme concept of what ice swimming would do to a person. That's the sort of thing where the mere attempt is enough to prove someone as a badass, never mind actually succeeding. But for ice swimming, I personally imagine two prongs of appeal: toughness, and masochism. Both are extremely rare and proportionately sexy, in my opinion.

If any females out there see this and start producing the right juices as a result, you know how to respond. That's also part of why I looked into MMOs. I've seen the legends, of partnerships formed in such virtual universes. Sadly, to this day, they remain just that: legends. It's the sort of thing you'd tell your kids for a bedtime story, right alongside your favorite brand of mythology or whatever misadventures your otherwise routine errands had procured. What's important is that I still remain sadly single, though fully aware there are worse outcomes than being single and sad. Doubly since I've given up on the dating sites, because I got sick of all the bible thumpers and dog humpers. (Both of which, by the way, could make for valid enemy types in either this game or its hypothetical sequel!)

But, as for the here and now, the human mind was not designed to be turned off for such extensive periods. I need stimulation and excitement. So, that's part of what's pushing me back towards work on my game, doubly since I am specifically itching to make productivity fun again. 

11:20 PM, almost midnight, I *WAS* planning on getting back into the saddle, though I feel *slightly* off, probably because I was a little late in keeping the vertigo in check. Plus, computer has more updates to do. Meaning, especially how I know "excitement agitates symptoms", I'm not sure about focusing on drawing at this time. A shame!

12:10 AM, almost 1 hour later (of social media, updates, and thinking), I feel like I should look up a couple very specific South Park references to get into the mindset of "Butt Probes". I mean I sort of see it in my head, but I very much want a frame-of-reference to work with.
12:15 AM, got a mild headache, but I think I can work through it if I'm slow and careful. Not ideal when trying to have fun depicting butt-probes, but I still think it's doable. Starting the process of making the title screen for V0.3 now! 

1 AM, got decent progress while snickering the whole way through. Trying to give Scarlet this sadistic yet enticed look on her face as she's about to do the honors of violently probing one of the captured invaders. And the way she holds up this magenta object, it's like a paladin going all "Feel the Power of Thy SWORD!" Yes, that's a heavy metal reference. Look it up. The metal by itself is badass and awesome, but it's so crazy funny to me in this specific context of a 5-year-old girl violently butt-probing an alien invader! 
God, now I'm tempted to make a whole scene of Scarlet against the aliens, and having a secret alternative to the knife be a dildo, and for beating the whole chapter (like Chapter 7 or 8) with just that, and having a special achievement for it called "The Power of Thy Sword". Also there'd be a special soundtrack check for, "IF Scarlet is wielding Dildo, THEN play Jay's version of 'Power of Thy Sword', ELSE play the normal Chapter Song".
Of course, I'd first have to revamp the knife mechanics and implement glory kills or similar features to make the knife useful. One other problem: the dildo finishers need to be of a different animation from the knife finishers, so...one thing at a time. Focus, we're drawing the V0.3 title screen right now. (Well, TRYING TO, when I can get past all my laughing, daydreaming, and juvenile snickering)
As for Scarlet's probe sword, I wanted it colored magenta for a reason. In video gaming culture, when something is just plain magenta, not the stylized sort we see in big budget games, it usually means "texture missing" or the texture *is* there but the computer is not commanded correctly to look where it's supposed to, similar to how the T-Pose is when a 3D character model has no animation or something broke in the code and thus the computer falls back onto a default state. The only difference is that here, it's no error, it's done on purpose as a silly chuckle to reference such goof-ups in the gaming industry.
(The ACTUAL "texture missing" is a checker pattern of magenta and black, and that's MUCH HARDER to implement than just plain magenta.)

1:35 AM, I think I am almost done (tm) with drawing the title screen. Many of the design choices directly reference the old-school South Park, namely their very first episode "Cartman Gets an Anal Probe". I really like the simplicity of the show back then, and how that makes everything more adorable. The new stuff is still good, and while the art direction is gorgeous there, I personally liked the cuter, old-school better. Just a matter of opinion, since it matters for the context of explaining what inspires Short Bus.
After subtracting breaks and distractions, probably took about 30-60 minutes of real work so far. 

2 AM, I'm losing focus. Feeling a bit "bleh" too. But at least the title page is mostly done. Just have to add a few colors and try to redesign the logo, since what I currently have feels very placeholder. Just gonna clock it at 1 hour of work. 

That aside, there are 2 points I checked on. First, most of the games I'm super excited for are still in PENDING limbo states. On the other hand, the achievement stat for The Way of the Badass has changed (used to be under 10%, now it's at 35.7%), meaning people *ARE*, in fact, playing my game. That's incredible.

(1 nap and lunch later...)
I still don't feel it. I know I felt it a day or 2 ago, meaning I guess I should just go grind until my brain pleads to do something creative. I regret not striking on that impulse at the time, but I was too focused on reaching my goals of the time.
Funny timing, even *that* game is going through an imminent update, so now's not a good time to grind, either. 

8:10 AM, MMO servers doing weekly updates, so...guess it's time to get back to drawing. And I keep laughing because of "THEY WILL KNOW THE POWER OF MY SWORD!" By itself, the song at face value is badass...but what makes it funny HERE is the context of Scarlet wielding her butt-probe, holding it high, the same way the paladins would point their blades of heroism to the heavens. Blending that imagery, with that music...THAT is what I find so funny.
Also those metal album covers are starting to inspire me to design a "not-placeholder" LOGO for the game!

8:50 AM, new dialogue box. This will happen right when you beat Chimera, so that Scarlet informs the player it's time to head back to the Badass Bunker for more character development and, more importantly, that's where Chapter 3 will transpire. Remember that panel to the left of the foyer? Yeah, that's now going to be implemented as the holding room for any captured survivors. And it's part of where Scarlet will do her probing and intrusive psycho-analysis. 
Mua hahaha!

9:10 AM, after about another hour or so of creative energy, I feel the need for another break. I lost my momentum, and I need to decorate the setting of the room where all the brain invading and butt probing will transpire.

10:15 AM, let's get started on that new dialogue box.
10:25 AM, the box is drawn, so including the slow-downs from low energy, took about all of 10 minutes to go from start to finish. Though, with that all said and done, I definitely feel another urge to just conk out and get ready for bed. Caffeine and metal music can only keep a person awake for so long until the inevitable happens.

There's one other problem. Feels like, I can't regain any of my energy, no matter how much I rest or eat. And this means it's hard to do *anything*, work OR play.
On top of that, at 11PM or so, Wednesday night, the whole house stank with overwhelming skunk. Even my gas mask was only partially effective at filtering it out!

Thursday...
I just wish everyone could shut up. I am simply done. I ran out of patience for all the bullcrap back in 2020. Not only am I having internal struggles with focusing, I also have to endure loads of rambling and futility behind-the-behind-the-scenes, which adds layer upon layer of "I can't bring myself to work on the game like I'm supposed to be doing." Part of me feels like I'm making excuses, but every gut instinct is like, "I'm done. I can't take all the mind-numbing crap of reality." 

In all seriousness, tell me what you think of the new logo. I seriously want something that says "badass" but I'm having trouble with how specifically to convey that. We can all agree that some of the original logos are mere placeholders. 

Friday...
OK, if there are no more skunks, stinks, MMO fixations, annoying family, bachelor blues, berserker boner, medical concerns or maintenance appointments (a.k.a. BREACHES OF QUARANTINE), energy shortages (electricity and human energy), or any number of ideas in my imagination that I find distracting, it's time to focus on finishing this up for the time and getting a move-on! 
Just know that when I have been saying there's been difficulty focusing, I am not joking!

2:50 AM, back in the saddle!
3:15 AM, backgrounds are simple and basic, but mostly passable right now. Later there's going to be more dialogue, the music shop opening, and new codex entries for the Chapter 2 Boss Fight. All of that will have various checks from new variables to make sure it's all in line with the story's progression. But that's not for today, just know that's on the to-do list.
3:35 AM, let's get this all saved into more universal file formats and over to the game engine. 

I think everyone's going through an overwhelming whirlwind of crap right now, and while we all deal with it differently, we all have the same problem: too much crap, all happening too fast. For me, I'm trying to tell everything to shut up, but that's only getting so far. 

3:40 PM, one other point for the near to-do list...I need the Chapter 3 Title Card! 

4:05 AM, let's test the new room.
Had to clean up some old residue from the V0.2.1 launch screen. 
4:10 AM, new door is not working. We are specifically at a point where the Chapter 2 Boss should be dead, and the global variable for "Chapter 2 Beat" is now flagged to greater than zero (which is just a roundabout way of telling a boolean to read as "true"). So, for debugging, we'll make the invisible door object visible.
ALSO I'm not sure if the secret shortcut is despawning when it should be. 
That said, the new door is not being made visible, so I'm led to imagine it's not spawning.

4:15 AM, debug tells me that killing the Chapter 2 Boss Fight is NOT triggering a "Chapter 2 Beat" condition. What we need is, "IF all 3 boss bad guys are dead, THEN declare Chapter 2 Beat as greater than zero." 
On the bright side, it is FUCKING AWESOME watching the Colonel just RIP AND TEAR through the boss fight, making it look like the chimera enforcers get shredded if he so much as SNEEZES at them! It also makes debugging more effective and entertaining, since we can jump right to the condition check without having to do the "actual, proper boss fight". It's all part of why having access to him so early counts as a cheat.
4:30 AM, now it's working. Got distracted daydreaming for a few minutes also, and I didn't even need to get rid of the "End of Demo" pop-up.
