notes.title: Scarlet Dev Diary Day 87
notes.notes:
Day 87

The game's out on Steam! Already, a mere day or 2 from that point, I got my first review on Steam! It's written by some what I think is Russian (no idea how they got through my language barrier, but good on that character), yet the important part is the thumbs up. That's a start, but both Steam and myself are fully aware it's going to take more than 1 review to get put on the map! Though, in addition to that, I even got an email from a "curator" to review it. For those who don't know what a "curator" is, it's essentially a more formal organization for doling out reviews. This is what I want. 
I have no idea where this adventure will take me, but all I know is, I have not been this charged up since I toured Comic Con back in 2013! It feels amazing to have that hope of awesomeness! Even if it's an illusion slated to be shattered in a year or 2, I'm enjoying living in the now.
I mean, what the fuck is happening?! I've got a British marketing team and a musician all asking to contribute to my work! I know birthdays are magical times (writing this on June 10), but seriously:
WHAT, THE, FUCK!
I mean that in the most positive, electrifying way possible! I need an extreme, exclamatory expression of excitement! 
Though, I need to be clear about this: for this SPECIFIC game, I want to do it ALL BY MYSELF! That's doubly because of the prominent zero-dollar budget! What this means to any would-be talent coming my way, is that I may be open to collaboration in the future, or for separate ventures. Just, not this specific one.
If you insist on lending a hand for a new game or similar, I sure hope you're able and willing to work FOR FREE! If not, then for now, don't waste my time.
So, for Saturday, I don't know if it's a sugar crash or whatnot, but I do feel "kind of bleh". It's the sort of day where all I want to do is laze around and cuddle day and night. Or play my other shooter games all day. Because I'll always have that itch to put bullets into bad guys! >:D
Also more game engine updates, but that is hopefully mild.
About Noon on Saturday, I tried taking a screenshot for the weekly, abridged Dev Diary. While doing so, the game engine felt like it needs to vomit every time it goes through updates. And, there's a reason I wanted to make a very specific dialogue box bigger (mostly for cheat mode). 
12:25 PM, after the game engine got done vomiting, it spawned a bug with the dialogue variable check not being reset to 0 with starting a fresh game. 
12:40 PM, one headache later, and I've started debugging that dialogue variable. Apparently, returning to menu with F1 does NOT reset it to 0, which is weird considering I don't remember that being a save mechanism. Thankfully, loading again fixes that, so it's not an issue right now.
Then I went for another break after I got the screenshot I wanted.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/a576fd859f0fc565828769b05ef0c680650755de.png[/img]
 
I need to put the voices on my to-do list, even though I'm yawning at 2PM. Would be the perfect opportunity if I weren't feeling so drained and lazy on this Saturday afternoon.

(Sunday...)
Ah, what a wonderful day for Prayer Day! And of my single-digit following, nobody's going to get that reference. I'll give you a hint: it's from a niche RPG.
Now then, Scarlet's Diary!
12:40 AM, let's see if I can do it for serious this time. (I was also thinking about the Codex book having hotkeys 1 through 4 to jump around the different sections, with 0 going to the table of contents, as a shortcut for all the clicking that'd be needed for flipping through all the pages.) 
12:50 PM, speaking of references, nobody's going to get the reference at the end of the Flamethrower's codex entry. "Napalm sticks to kids", look it up. It's from the Vietnam decade, so unless you're a living Boomer or WW2 veteran, chances are it was before your time. All you need to know is, it is dark and it is badass.
Sometime later, I really want to bring my writing powers to bear by focusing on character chemistry. But not this time.
1:15 AM, I got distracted for about a quarter hour. Finished the flamethrower page, then my curiosity about cartoon characters on social media threw off my groove. See, it's hard enough to stay focused when I don't have irritations physically knocking on my lair's door. 
1:40 AM, after fire and acid are done, now we're getting to my favorite: COVID! And yes, NOW we're REALLY getting to the LORE of the game!
I don't care what parts of the game you see or skip, but this is absolutely one that I MUST highlight:

2:10 AM, and there's 1 weapon to go (2 if you count the S.S. FUCK YOU!). Oh, and for funsies, the Colonel's special Rail Rifle gets a mention, for lore reasons. Yeah, a good way to summarize this entry is "MORE LORE!" 
2:50 AM, made some progress, but it's hard to not get distracted because I'm laughing so hard about COVID and SCHOOL being these epic forces! 
3:30 AM, almost done with Colonel's Gun, but the distractions are piling up, and I  feel the urge to take a lunch break...assuming COVID itself is not in my house. 
4:15 AM, break's over. Let's see if I can get back on track, though I'm not feeling too sharp right now. Let's try and finish this up, just with Colonel's and Violet's guns, then off to implement in the game engine. 
4:45 AM, work takes a while mostly because I'm enjoying the groove, and really deep in thought on how I can inject Scarlet's Codex/Diary with LORE! Seriously, those who comb through it at length will find some "fun facts" about the universe and how this alternate timeline ties into the REAL world. (Some of the most enjoyable flavor text, however, is "encrypted" by Scarlet's handwriting, in ancient runes only the educated nobility can successfully transcribe.)
5:10 AM, changing my mind...there's 2 more weapons I want to give special mention: Earnest's "FUCK YOU" missile salvo, and the M117 Swagger dubbed the "Queen of the Rifles". 
5:35 AM, OK guess I'll leave Amanda's for later and meet myself halfway. Enough drawing and writing, let's try and add all this new good stuff to the game! That's 8 pages into Scarlet's diary codex drawn. Would've been 9 if I could stomach the Swagger, but as I said, that'll have to wait for another day. I'm already not too far from a full-time shift this Sunday. 
And this is where all the "if-then" nesting gets really complicated. There needs to be one for each weapon.
5:55 AM, the thing to remember about this nesting is that the "right clicked" section should decrease while the "left clicked" should increase, and try to keep them organized based on "which page should come right after; if that one is not unlocked, then check for the second-closest, and so on". It's dawn, I see the subtle light out my window, and here I am dragging and dropping code logics. 
6AM, that should take care of all the "right page turns", so now we can test if this idea works. Left page won't work right now, but I'm not testing that for now. This is also going to presume that cheats are used and everything's already unlocked.
And yes, everything works, first try. Now for left clicking, it's likely the same just in reverse. 
6:05 AM, everything works! Again, first try! Though, for a REAL challenge, I'd have to test a "Fragmented" approach - like what if someone unlocks one companions but not the other? I can't be bothered to do that right now, so to wrap up, I'm going to add codex shortcuts for each of the 3 or 4 sections. I say "3 or 4" because the missing 4th is "Neutral", which would have entries on bystanders like Tom and Heather. But because those characters are not yet incorporated into the Codex/Diary, this whole section is currently "Not Applicable". 
It's not yet clear in-game, but the shortcuts go like this:
0 "Table of Contents"
1 "Section 1 Good Guys"
2 "Section 2 Neutral"
3 "Section 3 Bad Guys"
4 "Section 4 Weapons"

6:33 AM, man...I could really feel my brain going "Bleh" and numb near the end of that, but now, it's time to test it. If this looks good, then it's time to get the video ready for you, and along the way of sending out this Dev Diary, I'll have to (hopefully briefly) clear my inbox. Gonna be honest, I somewhat get nervous, because each time I go there, it's a gamble of "nothing at all", "scumbags", or very rarely one of you showing support for me. 
Thank goodness, looks like it's all working. Recording time.
Also thankfully, emails today are looking quiet. Could've gone worse, to be honest...could've gone better, also, but absolute silence is (for good AND for bad) par for the course. Maybe because it's the weekend, but whatever the reason, it's comparatively relieving. 
Though looking through old-ish emails, Steam had closed my ticket about the game build with saying that German law "may prevent" the display of swastikas. That's fair, though I do not apologize for that because part of my artistic vision is to take the ballsy route of making an antihero out of what mainstream sees as villainous (even if for fair reason). So screw Deutschland, they can censor my game all they want, as my creative freedom and standing by that is far more important to me. Besides, not like I was ever planning on translating this outside of English, anyway! 
(Yes, I know, the whole goal of this game is to punch censorship in its metaphysical, nonbinary face. Well, unless I were actual god-tier like the fictional Colonel, I don't see how I can beat a whole culture's wincing towards its own history.)
Point is, as long as I can do my own thing, I really don't fucking care!
Back on track, for final distribution on Steam's end...I noticed there's a consistently single-digit number of people who actually READ the Dev Diaries. 

Last time I put it publicly on Youtube, but sometimes, it has stuff in it that may not go on such a highly prudish territory...which is why I take the (SLIGHTLY) more private avenue of cloud storage instead. That's what this link is for. It's this entry's video!
[url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1CEtV1_ydwqoMvjimp9tdHu9Z0sujycMr/view?usp=sharing]https://drive.google.com/file/d/1CEtV1_ydwqoMvjimp9tdHu9Z0sujycMr/view?usp=sharing[/url]

And now, I return to rest and playing video games...shooting terrorists for fun.

I really need to cuddle with an adult human female. What does it take?!

notes.title: Scarlet Dev Diary Day 86
notes.notes:
Day 86

Given the headache from trying to get the rails to properly spawn out of the barrel of the rifle, this time I wanted to shift to something more fun. Maybe I'll add the alternate dialogue for playing with all companions from the start (though for that, the sound department recommends I wait for when everyone's awake), or expand Scarlet's diary (since it does not go into detail for all her weapons). Another idea I liked is to again take a page from Metro Exodus, with a Gameplay toggle option for "Creator Commentary", to spawn a few interactable objects that would play some voice lines from me that would point out some of the more exciting highlights to making the game. 

2:50 AM, good morning, Wednesday! Let's get started!
3AM, game engine update! Also I'm focusing on the alternate dialogue, plus coding in all the unlocked companions so they show up inside the Badass Bunker. 
3:10 AM, gonna need some more dialogue variable checks for all the bonus dialogue. Same sort of setup that I had with Duke's introductory talk. And also, a branching check in the middle of that discussion, to see if you're playing with all companions unlocked. As I said, doing that completely rewrites the story, and I meant it.
3:20 AM, testing to see if the new behind-the-scenes objects spawn companions inside the Badass Bunker. Everyone applicable should be visible once you use the "All Companions Cheat". Some are in the Armory, others in the Bunk. Game engine has to rebuild the whole game because of the update, and since it was not intended for cartoon graphics but for pixel graphics, that means it takes a couple real minutes for that to get done. Maybe it's not the game engine's fault, maybe that's just a physical limitation of computer technology of the time. I have no idea. 
I'm thinking about taking Duke out of the bunk, since he's also in the foyer. 
For the test, they're all working...except Karl, and I'm not sure why. Also I want to put the companions on a different layer, so that rather than Scarlet being all superimposed flopping 2D image on top of 2D image, maybe we'd have the illusion of her walking behind them. The illusion only works for characters at the bottom of the room, and the opposite is true for characters at the top. Characters in the MIDDLE will COMPLETELY break the illusion. 
At least I figured out why Karl wasn't loading in. He'd get deleted, as the original Obj_Karl was used for other purposes, rather than the placeholder state of the other companions. SO, to not interfere with the structure I had for Karl elsewhere, I created a separate "Obj_KarlBunk", deleted all the code in the new copy, and told the bunk spawner to point to that new object. 
3:30 AM, after a couple minutes of tweaking precise coordinates, the companions are LOOKING GOOD! 
1 hour of work, and already I've got the companions to spawn in the bunker, plus I've gotten Duke's alternate dialogue working for all companions. No voicing, because it's too early in the morning and I don't have the isolation I need to get loud at all hours I desire. 
Now Duke's dialogue was easy to implement since the variable and most everything else was already implemented. Building whole new dialogue chains for each companion is very tedious, but clearly doable. Especially now that I know how to make it work, thanks to Duke. 
4AM, gonna need to recharge the creative juices for writing. Got a little dialogue with the Colonel, but I wanted to do something more with the chemistry of Violet, Earnest, and to scheme up something obscenely goofy for Super Hobo! 


So I got a little caught up with watching Youtube (by about 4 hours), as the writing groove hadn't yet come. But that's OK, because while thinking about some ideas on the official Discord server, I was looking ahead to a month from now, daydreaming about a live Q&A session doubling as creator commentary, to give a tour of the game as it'd stand at that point in time. It'd be a good chance for scumbags to crash the party, but that's a risk I'm willing to take. While there's no rigid schedule, I imagine it'd go about 15-30 minutes, and be fossilized on the publicly visible parts of Youtube for historical preservation. 
Point is, it'd be very cool to see how much could get done in 1 year of zero-dollar budget and part-time schedule, with this completely "When I Feel Like It" attitude to creation. 
So, at 8:05 AM, I got a bit of writing for Violet and Colonel. Not a lot, mind you, but it's enough to get started with some flavor text in this alternate playthrough. The next step was obvious: giving dialogue boxes for them. No sound this time, for behind-the-behind-the-scenes reasons. 

And yes, Scarlet CAN hug her father the Colonel!
 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/4c4fb30d334ec2eb889530af5a720a6af3f2de70.png[/img]

2 hours of grooving with drawing, and got some dialogue cooking here with the Colonel. Again, early happy birthday and all that. I've got other plans for today, so I'm hoping that I have enough time to get this in-game, voice or not, and send today's Dev Diary to you. This will show a good pace for progress over one real day, not the whole half-month time warp we've seen with Dev Diary Day 85.
10:45 AM, finishing up Colonel's Chapter 1 dialogue, the sort of thing you WON'T see without the All Companions cheat. 
10:50 AM, now let's get these new dialogue boxes implemented in-game! Gonna have the check systems in place so when Scarlet's sprite is colliding with his, press F and it should start the chain.

I count 9 dialogue boxes done in 1 day, taking about 3 to 5 hours of effort grand total (not counting the 4 hour break I had in the middle there).

11:10 AM, OK got the base code structure. Let's test this, see if the Colonel's willing to talk.
First try, it ALMOST works! Last dialogue box just keeps jumping to Scarlet, and won't delete until after she's moved a ways from her father. 
I guess I really DO need that dialogue variable, after all. AND add it to the ScarletBoots.ini so that it gets saved.
11:20 AM, everything works! Got all the read-and-write bits for the menu buttons, Scarlet's save and load hotkeys (F5 and F9 respectively), even the autosave in the foyer to the Badass Bunker! Wasn't particularly painful, either. And NOW, everything works 110% as intended!
So, with the clock running down on plans I have behind-the-behind-the-scenes, combined with all the effort it took to bring you 9 fresh new dialogue boxes, I'm going to call this a done day's worth of work, and prepare the video!

One more SUPER SHOCKING revelation! Just as I was going to copy-paste the Dev Diary onto Steam (since I promised they'd get the UNABRIDGED version), I found that the game build is APPROVED! The big green button saying "Release as Early Access"...given that we're 1 day away from my birthday, if this truly works, it's going to be incredibly cathartic! 

I'm hoping I'll have off with tomorrow, June 9. Why? BECAUSE BIRTHDAY! YAY! To think, I'll be 30! Looking and living like a teenager, this is how I'd want to live if it were sustainable. Sadly, reality hasn't dealt me that kind of hand. So, best enjoy it while I can before reality inevitably doles out a fate worse than death.

https://youtu.be/6IT5V-VouXU

See you anywhere from Friday to Monday, if all goes well. If not, well, that's why I say "When I Feel Like It!"

Semper Bellum!
Jay

notes.title: Scarlet Dev Diary Day 85
notes.notes:
Day 85

Steam had a few comments for rejection. The store page, at least the response I got was not completely hopeless; just a technical correction or three.
It was 1:45 AM, Sunday May 15, and when I was finishing up with some goals in video games (with mixed results), I noticed the Steam replies, and I could not sleep on that kind of suspense!

Second message, at this point all my nerves are really getting to me! On one hand, if I'm not crossing some kind of line, I'm not trying hard enough. On the other hand, always bet on disappointment, so I can't help but nonstop anticipate serious blockages. Either way, it's hard to think rationally, from both mild sleep deprivation and getting all worked up over this event in my life.
3AM, and that's 1 of 2. Now I need to find where the save of "scarletboots.ini" is kept locally. I know I looked that up somewhere else; it just slips my mind and I can't be bothered to dig through loads of dev diary for it. 
AppData / Local / The_Way_of_the_Badass
Here's hoping I try to remember. But for now, since I'm still in talks with the Valve and Steam team, I want to keep my build of the game consistent with what's in their hands. Meaning there will be no more changes to the game (and no more actual concluded entries of this Dev Diary) until either my game goes live, or that effort is completely FUBAR. 
First impression says that, as of this weekend, it is not yet hopeless. Given my lecture about "the difference between hard and hopeless," that is encouraging.
4AM, about 2 and a quarter hours of work on this. The things we do for love. Should take a couple days, but this came back to me faster than expected. As I said, to make sure we're all on the same page, there will be no more changes to my game for the short-term future. 

(Wednesday, May 18, 2022)
HOLY SHIT! The moment I sent the email of the store page going live (with the game portion still taking more extensive review by the team...fingers crossed but anxiety welling up), I wasted no time in starting to build my presence over on Steam's Discussions forums! I really wanted a booming and powerful "Hello", so I will be saving that as a separate document, because like ALL my writing, it is (in my highly biased opinion) a work of literary art. And I will share that with you, since I can't presume you all have full access to Steam (or are not willing to make yet another username and password to add to the long list).
Took me about 2 hours of effort setting that up. And it was extremely fun, testing things out and starting to build my presence. Question is, how long will this last before I get into trouble for any number of censorship reasons?
2:20 AM, I got introduced to the censorship robot on the forum discussion. I know I've seen it before, but this is the first instance of it trespassing in the Kingdom of Badass! If there's no way for me to turn it off, I can at least draw a cute cartoon demonstrating what I mean by "public executions". Don't worry, no real-world harm is intended even here; it's just a cartoon.

(Friday...)
Overall, it's been a very quiet week. The news of my store page has got me extremely excited, though I've only got congratulations from a friend or 2, and that's it. I don't think anyone new has been roped in, even if some of the market images are admittedly placeholder. But I don't think that's the main reason for such anticlimax; I really think this is the par for the course. 
The game build ITSELF is still in a limbo state to my understanding, relative to Steam allowing it to go live and be downloaded, and as I posted on social media, no change will be brought to the game until after either my full game goes live, or the effort proves futile. This is to make sure the platform and I  remain on the same page about the exact state of the game. It's been a good excuse to watch Youtube, though I'm itching to get back to creating for this game - specifically, filling more of Scarlet's Diary with lore and for starting work on Chapter 3. 
For what-if, when or if that game goes live, the basic call to action for you is simple: download and play the game, review it (good or bad, either way, just be honest), and tell everyone you can about it. Without that, I'm stuck shouting in a vacuum like I've been doing ever since, approximately, 2010.
Communication is key. It's not just me posting these to you, it's equally important that YOU talk to ME! There was a time not too long ago, in the COVID era, I felt like I was living in solitary. That may not be the case NOW, but let's prevent that from happening again. OK? 

(Monday...)
So, May 23, and I gave a nudge to Steam, specifically the open and pending support ticket for them reviewing the game build. I promised to not change the game until either the build goes live, or the effort proves futile. And the fact I got my store page up to the public indicates that this is not yet completely hopeless. Even with one real week of silence on Steam's end, which is why I felt it was fair to give them a friendly nudge.
OH, and someone put my game on wishlist. What the fuck?!

(June 3, 2022...)

My GOD, it's been weeks and weeks of delay. And only now did I try to download the game from Steam, which believe it or not, actually worked. Full details here, both the good and the bad.
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1998760/view/3372646384225668845

As I said there, it's almost birthday time, so...like I did with Violet in March, I'm going to shunt the priority list by adding a very special companion you can cheat in.
2:15 PM, clearing a backlog of messages, turning social media off, so I can focus on drawing! Put on that music!
2:20 PM, let's get started!

There are also 2 sound effects I want to create for this: the FOOMP sound of heavy metal sabatons charging to battle, and the BOOSH sound of the Rail Rifle Mark 2 (codenamed "Faderator" in honor of a special debug weapon of Fallout New Vegas). Both of which need to be fitting for the "King of Badass" and the "King of the Rifles"!
3 PM, about 4 frames of animation for the Colonel facing right. I really wanted to give this vibe of "a spring in his step" and, more importantly, the "leaping into action" vibe! MOST characters get about 3 frames of animation, but the Colonel deserved a little better, so I gave him 5. 
3:15 PM, I like the jiggly physics. Counterintuitive to wearing full metal power armor, but it's extremely cartoony and animated. Though in practice, he looks less like he's charging into action, and more like the march of a Terminator. Still cool, just not QUITE what I was going for!
Time to do it again, for him facing LEFT! 
3: 50 PM, left side is now looking good enough, first impression. 
4 PM, good enough. Now, time to code him in, and add the ammo type: the signature RAIL! For funsies, I took a picture of my arm, and drew the cartoon Rail on that image, just to give you the canonical proportion of what he's supposed to be firing. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/9b931a1d80829944e94281d57eabee06c6a2f8bf.png[/img] 


Next, was sounds. The iconic *TOOM* sound of the Rail Rifle needed to be captured. My voice, as with many sounds, was the starting point. I tried distortion to various levels, which did have a decent "crunch" sound, but it didn't have that heavy-hitting vibe. What really got closer to the mark was when I cranked up the bass to ultra levels. Even subtle levels of distortion create a pixelated sound, which is NOT the right vibe for a rapid-firing Rail Rifle! 
4:30 PM, sound balancing to see how the sound effects stack up with the rest of stuff in game, I used the debug key for "Press Button to TOOM!" 
And debug key is not working. Tried a different sound effect, still had no sound. Sound works when I tell it to happen when knife spawns, so that's weird the debug key won't make it work.
5 PM, had some interruptions, and I'll have to think about the sound for the metal footsteps, but for now, I want to focus on coding in the Colonel! So that with access of the cheats menu, he can be totally playable as a companion! 
Then I realized, I'm going to need a reload animation for the Colonel! One thing at a time...let's first get the basic model in-game. 
5:35 PM, most of it is copy-pasted code from what I had with Violet, just deleting the grenade segment (not applicable) and changing "LMG Bullet" to "Rail", or similar matters. Also I'm setting the Rail speed to 250 instead of 300, because combine that with the much larger sprite, and I'm hoping to slightly mitigate the "flying sword physics" that the game engine employs for sufficiently fast objects. It's not like a bullet as you'd think of it streaking through air. It's like it jumps from point to point, and never touches anything in between those jumps, BUT if it moves SLOW ENOUGH, it creates the ILLUSION of normal movement. "Flying Sword" is a reference to Myth of the Epic Force since that's how the spacecraft of the 3 characters behaves.
I've been back in the saddle for 3 hours now, and I'm debating about taking a lunch / dinner break. Either way, I am so happy to be moving again!
Then I realized I was accidentally writing the code for Violet, mixing that up with Colonel. Oops. Big undo, coming up! After that, let's close up Violet's object window to prevent another misunderstanding.
6:15 PM, I think MOST of the coding is done now, particularly double-checking that it's for the Colonel this time. Meal break, then after the break, it'll be testing and debugging, and once that's working close enough, animate reloading and implement that.
6:50 PM, break's over. The one code I almost forgot is getting the companion room to add the Colonel.
7 PM, forgot the UI for City Streets 4 was turned off. Not sure if that made it into the main release...either way, that's the area of the first boss fight.
7:10 PM, no Colonel. Here we go again, back on the debugging rodeo. Debug menu is very interesting. It thinks that on main menu, there's a load of unneeded Charisma instances. 
7:20 PM, the break point for debugging shows that the if-then for creating Colonel instance IS being read, just no instance is actually created. Ammo variable is updated on the world map, but not before then, which is a bit weird since I tried loading all that in the frontend of the game's start. 
7:30 PM, well, telling the Chapter 1 manhole at World Map creates the Colonel instance, according to debugger. But for some reason, he doesn't survive past that. Let's see if making a Step check in Scarlet makes her summon her father more reliably. 
...NOPE! 
7:40 PM, making him a persistent object works. Good enough. Now just to tell him to get deleted whenever returning to the main menu. (He's already hidden, but this is more of a just to be sure sort of thing.) Now that the bulk of that is working, it's time to tweak the rate of fire for the rifle. 
7:45 PM, got a good image capture of the Rail Rifle, and I see a couple things. First, the space absolutely helps cover the ground of "Flying Sword" physics, so that's good. But, 1) each aril is bigger than the gun; 2) they originate from inside the Colonel, not his rifle, and 3) having it shoot too fast makes the firing sound effect come out like crap. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/45c91d43fd7566d979b8f8ba1c36378b670c80f1.png[/img] 



8 PM, I tried to run the game on Steam from an alternate account, and found that it only took me to the store page when I did. So, I guess playing proper through Steam is something only I as the developer can do, and that the true "Early Access" is still in limbo. 
And I've been at it for about 5 hours (6 grand total, before subtracting breaks), so with that disheartening revelation (and me trying to edit the original announcement has to go through more stringent checks than creating a whole new announcement), I think it's best to just  be done with it for now.

(Monday...)
Happy D-Day, everybody! For whatever reason, it just felt hard getting out of bed, but here I am. After a weekend of games, I wanted to try and finish what seems almost done. Also, I know how silly it is calling this one "day" when it took weeks of limbo, and half-complete portions that all spanned so much real time. Don't call me out on that, things didn't go to plan and impulses be that way with me. 
6:40 PM, let's get started! Tweaking the rails themselves is the first, easy step to get back on track. Smaller, more in front so it aligns with the rifle, that sort of thing.
The trickier part about rail positioning is that it needs to be slightly to the right, if he's facing right, or slightly left if he's facing left. One coverall will look weird when it's the other way around. 
6:50 PM, after skimming the manual, a "sprite_exist" piece of code exists in the engine, but I'm not sure if that means "If this specific sprite is happening right now", or "If this specific sprite just exists SOMEWHERE in the code AT ALL". It's one of those times where details do matter. 
7PM, a simpler way for getting rid of companions on the title screen (since the "persistant" flag means no number of delete commands are getting rid of them), is to move the "Instances" layer below the background and all the other stuff happening on-screen. If we can't clear it, we can at least give the ILLUSION that it's been cleared. Also, for debugging, I'm setting the rail speed a lot slower so I can better see where it's spawning at, relative to Colonel and his Rail Rifle. 
And, the debug shows that it's just spawning to the left. Speed set back to normal since I got the info I needed. And it only checks to see if the sprite exists ANYWHERE in the game code, which sucks for what I'm trying to do. Did I do anything different for Violet?
Doesn't look like it. And now I can sort of see why. It's going to take some notably more complex coding just to check if a character is facing left or right.
7:20 PM, at least now we mostly copy-pasted the clock-and-hand structure used for Violet to define rate of fire. Just change "Violet" to "Colonel", and tweak it as necessary so we get the feeling "just right". The Rail Rifle Mark 2 does NOT have minigun rate of fire, or else the "fire a shot every in-game frame of animation" could actually be fine as-is. 
I almost forgot about the sound effect toggle for the new Rail Rifle sound. 
That aside, bad news is that the check for the rail position is not working. It just has it shoot from his middle. Good news, the companion purge behind-the-scenes is updated, which DOES clear out excessive characters. Maybe I should put one of THOSE on the title screen. 
A funny idea I had just now was to rewrite the story based around whether or not the player uses cheats, particularly in context that the whole vanilla story is based on Scarlet looking for her dad, the Colonel. But if he magically spawns because of "cheats", that completely changes the plot...almost like an "alternate playthrough". So, later, I'd want there to be special dialogue for that. I've already implemented a proof-of-concept with Duke getting a couple special lines if he's present for very specific moments, so do a "Colonel_Get" check for certain key story points and have Scarlet say something different based on that. Fun!
7:30 PM, and then it came to me. What about the sprite "origin" point? Put that to the tip of the gun barrel. Positioning is good, but he kind of teleports when shifting from right to left, or left to right. Maybe if he instead goes from right to middle and then from middle to left...Nope, at least not yet. Was worth a try. 
7:45 PM, what if we have a separate, behind-the-scenes object that's invisible, it ghosts his movement, and that has the different origin that the rails are instructed to spawn from? Because using the actual, visible Colonel for such anchoring makes him teleport when changing directions. 
7:55 PM, it was easier to determine right from left with Scarlet because she relies on the mouse, since she's the player controlled character. For NPCs who are independent of player input, we can't always consistently rely on that frame-of-reference. 
8:10 PM, I give up...for now. Maybe some insight will beam me in hindsight, but for now, the implemntation is "good enough". I even got him to stay with Scarlet when pressing F9 to reload while out in the fields of action. More testing shows he's not firing at all the bad guy types.
8:20 PM, oddly things are kind of cool without having a reload or ammo feature implemented with the Colonel. Makes me wonder, maybe the bottomless magazines should also apply to companions. That could be more fun. But for another time, I hope.
8:40 PM, I had an idea, then I lost it. Rail Create commands: IF Colonel.x is greater than Scarlet.x, THEN  jump to Colonel.x+50; ELSE IF Colonel.x is less than Scarlet.x, THEN jump to Colonel.x-50
8:45 PM, can't tell if it's working on the if-then checks, but CAN tell that a straight-up "jump to y-50" puts the shots more at the gun's level, instead of firing down from the magazine. 
9PM, see the -150 variable has the rails spawn just a little too far to the Colonel's front. Still a little wonky on the harpie room, but the pussy room it's spot on. 
So, about another 2.5 hours added to the work clock here. NOW I'm done, with it kind of wonky but also sort of "good enough for now". Maybe we'll come back for these tweaks around V0.9 but for now, I need to get a move-on. 

And, with all that done, here's the first post-Steam Dev Diary entry! For the two or three who've joined me from Steam, welcome. https://discord.gg/aXeHswSNS2 for an ALL-NSFW location to hang out and talk about the game, or see what other scumbags enjoy pestering me. 

That all done, let me leave you today's video. The Colonel is springing into action!
https://youtu.be/Or64cFuka84

See you in...HOPEFULLY a few days. But for now, I need to wash away all the scum and disappointment that's clinging onto my short-term memory. (Brainwashing, maybe? Like, washing my brain...)

Semper Bellum!
Jay

notes.title: Game Build Actually Works!
notes.notes:
(Post-bulletin update: I tried to run the game on an alternate Steam account, to see what a different person's point of view would bring me. And doing so just took me to the store page. Extremely confusing! Sorry for any error I made in my original announcement.)

Hello once again!

For the single digit people following me, the one piece of good news I have is that, yes, I ran my game from Steam. The build page has said pending for weeks (and still does even as I'm writing this), but then, just now, I had the idea of "What would happen if I just...clicked that big 'Download' button on Steam?" Wouldn't you know, it actually downloaded, and I played the game!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/6fa976ce98a81b74cc4342cfb7a65cc830f5b90b.png[/img]

MEANING, whatever I'm seeing about "pending" in my administrative dashboard has been absolutely misleading and, more to the point, FALSE! Game as far as I could see is good to go in all its glory! That ALSO means I can get back to work on making more content! If all goes well, the first REAL Dev Diary post-Steam will be coming in a couple real days! I want to do something special for June 9, because of a very specific birthday coming up!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/70689dcb2aa5dbae8345076fa1373577f675837b.png[/img]

...OK, that ends the good news. Now it's the bad news.

Short of it, I'm worried that my story is going to be Phil Fish or Zoe Quinn all over again. For those who have no idea what I'm talking about, and are too lazy to go look it up on Google or whatever, short answer is that they were relentlessly pestered by the scumbags of the Internet, for doing nothing more than trying to make a video game (or something similar). 

I mean for torture's sake, I've been doxxed. No joke. I regret deleting the message as a kneejerk reaction to it (should've quarantined the channel instead, so I can point to it for formal reporting). Though last I checked, around the time I was writing this, the person's profile picture actually contains some very personal and private information. How's that for your figurative "smoking gun"?

If there's any comfort, 
1) there's a single-digit following at the time of this writing, so if I know who all specifically is getting in right now to cause grief, at least I don't have too many suspects. Probably just some kid who isn't even meant to be here at all (with this aimed at being an M or AO rated game once it gets more complete and I feel ready to send to the ESRB), or the handful of bullies who've been with me ever since 2014. God, feels like everyone who's anyone will inevitably be targeted by filth that makes any sane person wince or cringe.
2) Because the Kingdom of Badass is a KINGDOM, I have the power to permanently banish the fools dumb enough to test my patience. 
3) The people who ARE causing me grief, both directly and elsewhere on the web, do have a reputation for being scum. 

We've definitely seen some other characters who ALSO have unpopular opinions, plus others who on the surface appear OK but I still have a sneaking suspicion of them.

All of this, and I've hardly started! This is just from the 300 or so "unique impressions" and 10 "unique visitors" (those 10 are the ones who've ACTUALLY come to visit; the other 300 are those that Steam may have shown the game in a list but got glanced over or ignored for any number of reasons on the human end). The metrics have exceeded my expectations, even when we look past the filth.

If you were to ask, "How does it feel," my answer would be, "A bit like the initial leaping over the trenches of World War 1, whistle blowing and everything, only so far less deadly."

You can definitely make the argument of, "Well if you're trying to protect freedom of speech to ALL, including the most extreme nutjobs", to that I have to say, "As much as realistically possible." When it becomes a genuine problem, a line needs to be drawn. 

There's still a voice in my imagination saying something like, "You sort of ARE asking for trouble, what with the specific subject matter of this game." Honestly, yes and no. Yes because I do want to show off my steely resolve by defying all censorship, but no because...honestly, who WANTS to get harassed?

To wrap this up, you're welcome to talk about the game, or such...though given the kind of following I have, you may want to stay away from the social media channels for a while. I anticipate it's going to get worse before it gets better.

As for me, I refuse to cow to such pathetic attempts at undermining my creative passion! And now that I have found out that The Way of the Badass IS, in fact, LIVE...that means there is no more reason for any significant delay! Trust me, I am EAGER to get back to creating more for my game!

Semper Bellum!
Jay

Hello fellow Badasses and Wannabe Badasses,

Around the middle of May, there was a bit of back-and-forth between me and Steam's representatives. Nothing too overwhelming, just asking about one or two particular features, and I provided instruction on how to see what I was talking about. Then, things on their end went quiet.

I also promised to myself that, to ensure Steam and myself would be on the same page, that there would be no further changes to game development until either my game goes live, or the effort proves futile. Other than that, I will be doing everything I can to keep the spirit of awesomeness alive on my end. 

In addition, the store page should have links to Youtube and my ALL-NSFW Discord server, plus when I get done making this news update live, I'll be trying to add Twitter to that as well, so you can see some of my more controversial opinions about world events, as well as my perusing of cute cartoon characters, all in addition to the Abridged Dev Diary that comes out (ideally) every weekend. I'm afraid that for now, it's a package deal, so you get either all of that or none - depending on whether or not you choose to follow me there. As far as the personal sphere goes, I do operate in Maryland, USA, so if you somehow notice that this post goes out at weird hours, you can dispel your odd conspiracy theories of me being overseas; right now I'm simply nocturnal, and it's almost midnight my time while writing this. notes.title: Welcome to the Kingdom!
notes.notes:
Hello and Welcome, Badasses and Wannabe Badasses! 

Short about this whole thing is to introduce you to me, and to show you the way I think. Everything should be transparent whenever you want to pick my brain. Say hello whenever you get the chance.



I'm still learning how everything works on Steam, and the single biggest point so far is just how ABSOLUTE all the image dimensions need to be for it to accept them when being displayed. It feels like the first day on a job except it's a hobby I am super passionate and excited about! With that in mind, I feel like having a pinned Discussion or something similar would be a great way to give a first impression. Even if I don't interact with everybody, I do want to watch how everything transpires. Like the Almighty up above watching but not always intervening...that's what I want to be like, here.

As such, the way I'd run my Discussions if I possibly can, is about as Libertarian as possible. No banning or blocking, or any other such censorship, if it can be helped. Naturally, a line would exist somewhere...probably when things become a real headache or cause real-world problems. (And there are only so many times we can spin in circles before I run out of patience.) Just know I'm no guy in a tucked suit looking at the numbers more than the experience, and I mean it when I scream about wanting my freedom. I want to emphasize the *HUMAN* element to this universe!

There will be plenty of times I will hang out with the Community, whether that's on Steam, Discord, Twitter, or whatever site won't chafe with my...let's say, unpopular point of view. In fact, every weekend I will do what I can to give at least SOME form of contact (if not more frequently), just so you know that I'm alive and haven't forgotten about the game or any of you. (There's even a role-playing game that I host as Game Master, if any of you want a digital tabletop experience. It's normally set in my own wacky worlds, but sometimes I bring other franchises into that hobby...because it's fun to explore Star Wars, Powerpuff, Metro, Elite, South Park, and Paper Mario in the collaborative writing wonderland which defines the tabletop role-playing game experience. The best part? I try to keep all of those activities intertwined! It's something of a "Meta RPG" with how the tabletop game, the video games, and similar events all break boundaries and bleed over into one another.)

Because as this game will teach you, a Kingdom is no good if its King is MIA!
(Particularly with no real-world heir to cite, but that's a topic for a separate, less boisterous thread.)

[b]What can you expect from ME?[/b]

I did say on the store page about "Unabridged Dev Diary", and I mean it. All my family and friends have their digital copies to prove it. (I think the Dev Diary was at Day 84, so your FIRST taste of that will be Day 85). Each one of those chapters goes into every little detail, including what video game I was fixating on that kept me from working on this game right here. Much like this article here, you can expect the detail level to be enough to make all but the most devout feel their eyes glaze over. That's why I try to keep a sort of "In short..." bit at the top, or near the bottom. (Steam has a solid "Subtitle" and "Summary" pair for these kinds of postings, so that's also where you can enjoy a "TLDR" version.) Writing and fighting are my talents, so if you really want to read loads of paragraphs, then you're in luck, because the Dev Diary can count as a bonus free non-fiction novel, just for being a fan! (Showing I was not joking when I say that writing is one of my natural talents.)

[b]What can you expect from THE GAME?[/b]

The game will run, and as of May 2022, it is in a V0.2.1 state, "Steam First Contact Edition". Not much different from V0.2 except for a single digit number of bug fixes, and a celebratory title screen that super briefly shows all the main allies of the game. (Animation is crazy choppy, that's one of the new skills I picked up, namely since Adobe Illustrator was NOT intended for animation!) The game itself, while each and every "Dev Diary" will showcase all the proof of work, what will be put into YOUR hands will only be the major milestones (V0.3, V0.4, etc). That way, you don't have to keep updating the game every week or so, and Steam's cloud won't need to save a thousand different variants of subtle changes. 
That matters because I am planning on using the "Beta" feature for archiving previous milestones, so for historical preservation, even when or if V1.0 (the full release) is out being the definitive version, you can go back to V0.2 and see just how far things have come since then. Saves a lot of cloud storage on Steam's infrastructure to have 10 or so different game builds instead of 100 or whatever big number it'd take.
In terms of content, everything you see on the store page is everything I have planned and intended. Not all the features may be readily implemented as of V0.2.1 but most of them absolutely are! And it's certainly enough to give you an idea of what my artistic design is like. I have full "intellectual property" rights, the one human and not some corporate logo or brand. That makes me a "creative emperor", or living up to my "king" image since I want my franchises to stay very internally consistent and "in-character".

[b]What is the "Dev Diary" like?[/b]

Each entry will be a "News" article (though family and friends have the same or very similar experience, only by email), so it should appear at the absolute top of Steam's rows where all the other big features are. It will be similar to the girth of what is found here. First paragraph or two will show the human side, usually a bit of external gaming, who blocked me on social media this time over whatever misunderstanding, and so forth. Once pleasantries are done, we get straight into showing ALL THE WORK that goes into fixing those bugs, adding new features, or experimenting to see how I make something snazzier. It'll be about as unabridged as this post, so you can get a consistent idea of what you're in for as far as the "vibe" is concerned. Remember, it's ALL written by ME! I don't have minions or lieutenants, I'm just some guy who's having fun in his bedroom. No joke. Even my AD VIDEOS show that point! And I'm sticking with that as an artistic theme for this whole project, start to finish and beyond. (Other projects, we'll cross that bridge when we get there, but for now, this is all me and all just for fun. If you wanted to be the king of your own world, you go and build your own video game with your own original franchise...even if it's been inspired by what came before.)

[b]WHY am I making a "Dev Diary" that's practically the size of a classical literature epic?[/b]

Simple, I want something to show for all the time and energy I've poured into creating this brainchild of mine, and showing it to the public. I want it in UNABRIDGED detail so that if anyone who asks, "So, what was it like..." I can just quietly bring this digital tome out, and with no fanfare just drop it onto the digital table with a cartoony *THWOOMP* noise! Besides, in my imagination, this whole journey, the entire process of bringing this creation to reality, it's as close as I can realistically get to living a real-life EPIC! No exaggeration, compared to all the things I've done, both for hobby and for job, this is the single most stratospheric undertaking I have ever attempted! And I want that to show! (Even where success is not proportional to effort, at least there's proof of effort.) And finally, it tells myself that writing the stuff is by far the easiest and most fun part of my creative process. Yes, I have fun in writing the Dev Diaries, and I'm having fun writing THIS, the whole heap of words you are reading now. 

[b]SO! How can you help?[/b]

Here's what you can do:

1) Spread the word! The one thing I need is to get more people on-board with this, knowing that there's interest in what I have to offer to the world. 
2) Share your experiences! Give me your bugs, your suggestions, your...FEEDBACK! Whether you think Scarlet is the true ruler of the cartoon universe, or you think this all sucks monkey feces, I want to hear it all! The only wrong answer is no answer!
3) Review the game! I don't want to be like all the annoying clowns who squawk "LIKE AND SUBSCRIBE" all the time, it's that honestly, you can be the difference between "Positive", "Negative", "Mixed", or any of the extremes on that spectrum. That intensely matters when trying to stand out from the rest of the "meh" and be put onto the digital map! People sadistically (or masochistically) enjoy complaining about "Overwhelmingly Negative", just as much as they laud and celebrate each "Overwhelmingly Positive" title (which are almost consistently assured to define "mainstream" once they have that banner) but couldn't care less about "meh". And while seemingly every human prefers a positive outcome, I'd rather have a bad experience than a boring one. Above all else, BE HONEST! Don't go lying like if you thought things were bland, then don't go "review bombing" just to help me get noticed. There's a special place in the Devil's Dungeon for such liars. And it's not the D&D sort of dungeon, it's the sort that uses whips and tasers like toys on the imprisoned and condemned. And if you like the idea, you get to be Princess Scarlet's personal pain toy. So yeah, don't lie unless you want this cartoon, sentient plush doll to follow you whenever you get banished into the underworld's bowels.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42403007/728fd5d22eae67139466ae476d67738a90c97293.png[/img]
4) Have fun! That's what this is really all about. It's not about fame or fortune, even if both would be nice to have. It's about FUN! And freedom, too, but mainly fun! 



For now, get some rest, trooper. The ass-kicking begins hopefully real soon.

Semper Bellum!
The Golden Knight
Jay Geis
